analysis.name: Andrew Piletz
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 66 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Piletz is nice and cares about his students. The class is not unreasonably hard (homework is ~ one hour of lecture videos, one quiz, and a simulation assignment on connect). The exams are challenging but utilize exclusively application questions, so knowing word for word definitions is unnecessary as long as you understand the concepts.

This course was more difficult than I thought it would be, but Piletz was an awesome and engaging professor who made the class more fun. The timed and recorded quizzes every week, textbook readings and challenging exams were a bit annoying but if you study enough an A is definitely attainable. 2% extra credit is also offered.

In his smaller class sections you have to speak at least 3 times to even earn a B for participation which is kind of difficult in a class of 25-30 people. Also, his exams are pretty nit picky so you really have to study the materials to do well on them. His averages are pretty low for a marketing class (low 70s) so you definitely have to study lots

Great professor who truly goes above and beyond to know each of this students. Weekly quizzes can be frustrating but ultimately prepare you so well for the exams. Exams are tough but if you study getting an A is 100% do-able. Anyone who complains about Andrew or his class probably just isn't putting the work in to do well. Take him!!

Took honors. Class material was easy but we got through 90% of the 600 page textbook. Exams are more challenging but there are a lot of other grades and 2% of extra credit. Lectures were worth it but participating was required. Passed with an A- even though I got a little below average on every exam. Highly recommend!

analysis.name: Alan Pritchard
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great professor. Doesn't grade harshly on discussions and assignments, but the exams are very challenging especially if you take them in person and they are 80% of total grade. Provided EC opportunities. Lectures were very organized; it was just a lot of content to cover in half a semester.

Showing up to lecture and taking notes is the key to his class. Exams are worth 80% of the final grade so make sure you also attend during revision lectures as he could clarify about exams. Office hours are also helpful, he genuinely cares about his students.
He was a great professor. Really enjoyed his lectures. Exams could be a bit tricky, but if you study, you should be fine. He makes expectations very clear.

I am not fond of 1.5 hr classes. This class was all memorization and the exams (2) are worth 40% each. The exams consist of true/false questions with specific details from lectures. I struggled with this class and I'm glad it's over. The content was interesting however, I strongly disliked the exam layout. He also responds super late to emails.

The class was run incredibly well, the lectures were always pretty streamlined and the exam review sessions were incredibly helpful. Out of class assignments weren't too bad at all. The exams themselves are on the harder side, so definitely study a good amount for them. Would take another class with Professor Pritchard again for sure.

analysis.name: Amy Shuster
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I hate this class, there were so much materials to cover. Amy make the whole class into a whole wheel discussion for literally 2 hrs. Whether you want to talk or not, you have to discuss with others all the time, everyone was frustrated and super tired after this class. And she gave complicated assignments to waste your time.

She is a very tough grader on assignments that should be easy to get full credit on. She always posts her feedback late and expects students to know what is going through her mind. There is always a lot of outside work in this class when there shouldn't be and she takes this class way too seriously. Do not take this class, would not recommend.

She provides rubrics but doesn't seem to grade by them
She is a tough grader, even on draft assignments
Multiple times did not give 100's (This is a 1 credit hour course)
Incredibly nitpicky and wants assignments exactly to her liking
Usually barely in the room when class is scheduled or is flat out late

Dr. Shuster is very sweet. Many people in my class were confused but I think GE courses are always a little hard to follow because of the broad spectrum of content while keeping them 'introductory.' I would easily take a class with Amy again, they are extremely kind and good at giving you feedback on work/answering emails.

In Professor Shuster' class I felt safe to share. All opinions are welcomed and supported. Grades are generally based on completion of routine tasks. A knowledgeable philosopher with a really sweet personality.

analysis.name: Adeoye Oyeniyi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He was by far one of my favorite professors I have ever had! He is so so funny and so patient. He genuinely cares so much for each of his students and takes the time to make sure everyone is understanding. If you have the opportunity to take his class, PLEASE DO IT! The experience is irreplaceable :)

Taking ASL with Ade was the best decision I made last semester. Adding a foreign language on top of a pretty rigorous schedule was daunting to me, but I could not be happier with my experience taking ASL with Ade. Attendance is very important as the quality of his in-person teaching is irreplaceable by online video. He genuinely cares about you!

Professor. Oyeniyi was an amazing professor. His class is extremely fun and he genuinely cares about his students. My only minor issue was that dates of quizzes could sometimes be unclear but they were so easy it really didn't matter anyway.

He's one of my favorite professors. He genuinely cares about teaching and helping his students. He is deaf, so it makes you learn so much quicker because voices are off. He is super funny and I looked forward to going to class.

The best professor I've ever had! He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Very humorous and gives his own experiences as a Deaf person, it helped with understanding. A lot of class participation and some projects but overall great course.

analysis.name: Abraham Roth
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: A very questionable professor to say the least. I am not a fan of his teaching style, as he drones on for hours about how he wishes he was a worm eating glass. He often makes strange comments to the students, such as "Girls for the win smiley face emoji", and it makes a lot of the students uncomfortable. Don't take if you're looking for an easy A.

This professor makes very strict guidelines that are unreasonable and unnecessary. He expects the students to write like Descartes himself. Impossible to get an A in. Also he always smells like coins which is a bit strange if you ask me. He will occasionally ask the students for money, and if you leave anything on the ground he will take it.

Have you ever wanted to meet Helen Keller? If so, take this class and meet him for yourself. You will not be heard, seen, nor will he communicate with you. Doesn't not answer questions well, and when he does it's with sass and annoyance. Tough grader and expects you to write essays for easy written answer on homework or exams.

Great class. The most interesting part is that Dr Roth constantly complimented my love handles except they weren't body fat it was just pockets of water in my jeans. Unusual. I fully believe he intended on oiling me up after class, Very good teacher and gave me an A after that session.

Hope you like pediatrics because that's the only setting that exists here. Adult rehab? Never heard of him. Ask a question and get a sigh, a riddle, or a stare making you regret your question. Feedback is vague, grading is brutal, and clarity is a myth. 10/10 would cry again.

analysis.name: Andrew Heeszel
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is approachable and willing to help, but his exams are much harder. While homework and sample exams are recommended, actual exam questions often differ significantly in structure and difficulty. Concepts may seem familiar, but the problems require a much deeper understanding. As a result, doing practice problems alone is not enough.

I took this class during my last internship. While the homeworks were a bit tedious, he does give good feedback, was available for office hours / out of class interactions, and his modules were well organized. I did well taking this class across the country and online.

He did his best with a course none of the students wanted to be in. Lecture was kind of boring and recitation was not needed since nothing covered in recitation was useful. Easy class if you show up at all.

Andrew was the TA for Stat 4302, and yet he is the definition of Chadimus Prime.

 Andrew always tries to explain concepts from the start to end, this actually made understanding concepts more easier to me. He also graded assignments extremely fairly. He was basically a friend and I wish I went to more office hours.

Andrew might not be a perfect fit for everyone, but I got value from his lectures and learned the content well. Kind of gives ADHD energy, which worked well for me but not for others. Exams are exactly like the practice ones he posts, AND he allows you to make a formula sheet. Was able to ace both of the midterms and didn't need the final to pass.

analysis.name: Andrew Richards
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He is so bad at explaining concepts that even material I knew well from my physics and math courses seemed confusing when he explained it. Noone wanted to attend his lectures so he made lab attendance mandatory which was taught by an incompetent TA. Avoid if possible or just read the textbook if you can't and you will do fine.

Genuinely terrible, does not explain concepts and whatever he talks about in lecture does not show up in the homework or exams. If you like a professor that doesn't know how to teach, this guy is for you.

Lecture goes very fast and he spends time explaining things that don't even matter or come up in homework or exams. Very unsympathetic and not accommodating for students. Going to office hours was scary because he made you feel stupid for not understanding the material. The lab for this class was pointless because TA didn't know what he was doing.

Even basic statistics concepts will seem like a nightmare with him. Many did not do very well due to his poor teaching and yet he still refuses to curve the course (but instead made lab attendance required which was taught by a clueless TA). Completely unsympathetic and is very childish in his behavior. Avoid at all costs!

The powerpoints are provided beforehand, but you need to attend lecture to record the notes he adds during class. He does not record lectures, if absent you need to join the class zoom which is very annoying for an 8am class. He lectures very quickly as if students already know the material. Try to read the textbook before lecture. Good luck!!

analysis.name: Kaylea Annen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I loved Prof. Annen. The class was an easy A but who doesn't love that? There is a good chunk of work but it is not time-consuming, you just have to stay on top of the content. There aren't any major projects besides your portfolio, and you have plenty of time to work on it. She publishes all her online work early!

Idk why it's only 3.1/5 , should be 5. The only reason people shouldn't have a 100 in this class is because of the chapter quizzes, but even then they don't hurt your grade that much. Two speaking assignments and like 3 essays that aren't even longer than 3 pages double spaced. Super easy for the GE credit, really sweet and easy going professor.
She assigns a lot of homework. There should be a TA for her course
Don't take it if its for an easy A. She grades way to hard.

It is a GE course. I think she grade so hard on GE course and she rejected to reply to our questions before the due date. From my perspective, GE is more about expanding my knowledge. And the purpose of assginment is helping us understand the textbook better. Therefore, there is no reason to reject to answer questions before the due date.

analysis.name: Andrea Baldwin
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 378 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Class average on our last midterm was ~34%, she then spent ten minutes belittling us over how it was our fault and that we all weren't trying hard enough. Suuurely it wasn't the one thing all 300 or so students had in common (her.) She is inefficient in the classroom, and the flipped approach just makes at worse. If you want to learn ochem, run.

Baldwin tries her best but ultimately is not accessible outside of class and the tests are impossible. i tried to go to her office hours and there was always a line out the door and i had to wait like 45 minutes just to have one question answered. some of the tests had in the 30 percentage average (which indicates a teaching issue). good luck.

Provides way to much material, had a flipped classroom for my year that did not help at all. She will explain something once and proceed to go into a very complex problem and expect you to know it right off the bat. Acts as if her class is the only class you are taking.

She inefficiently utilizes the flipped classroom style. The tests are designed for you to get a C or below. To be honest, I'm not sure how anyone gets above that. I have disabilities and found this class quite inaccessible which was my downfall. Take it at CSCC.

I only did well bc I spent HOURS deciphering her 2x speed speech in lecture vids. Stay on pace the whole semester bc if you fall behind quizzes won't make sense. Don't take the practice exams, they will confuse you. Thoroughly watch the lectures and do every problem set and you will survive. Read the textbook if ur confused on something. Good luck

analysis.name: Billy Patterson
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 159 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: The exams are unfair and inconsistent. Studied hard for the first exam and did very well. Did the same process and more for exam 2 because I expected it to be a little harder but it was very unfair. The questions were completely different from all the questions we went over in lecture and recitation. Went from an A to a C.

Billy's exams has 5-10 questions we didn't do in lecture,hw, or recitation and he expects us to turnup and figure it out. He purposely made his exam impossible so he can meet his requirement from fisher to maintain a 75 average for the exam. He

Honestly might be the worst teacher I've ever had. His first semester at Ohio State was a dumpster fire and this one's not better. The overall average on the first exam was good, but the second exam was borderline impossible factoring in time and calculation problem difficulty. The class average was 23% lower than exam 1. Horrible Teacher.

Terrible. If over 40 people are giving awful ratings, I have a hard time believing that anyone but Billy would give a 5. Hopeful that he improves for the rest of the semester or the SEIs are going to be insane.

To the recent 5 rating of Billy. Wow you really love to have a superiority complex and stand out in the crowd don't you. No one asked for your kiss up opinion. I got a 100 on the first test and thoroughly studied the lectures and recitations for the second test and definitely failed. There was not nearly enough time.Stop making everything about you

analysis.name: Erynn Beaton
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I was able to get an A in the class. You have to participate in class. If you go to class and participate and talk with her, you will be able to do well. Overall, very interesting class.

Don't buy the textbook you can find a PDF online. I really enjoyed having Beaton as a professor, the class is valuable information, but she does grade writing harder than I think she should for a GE. If you're a business student I think this is a valuable GE that actually applies to your major.

Dr. Beaton is amazing. She is caring, attentive, and understanding. It is clear she really appreciates feedback and applies that to the course. Attend class and you will do fine. She uses TopHat during her lectures so you can get easy points from the readings.

Really cool and clearly cares about the subject matter. The class is pretty easy as long as you attend lecture and do the readings. Daily debates keep things engaging and are super useful to applying how to concepts we have learned are relevant to current events or policy in the U.S. Erynn is very understanding, and always willing to help students.

Professor Beaton is really easy-going and genuinely nice. The class is interesting, and she makes things less boring by adding debates. The reading is super light, and the papers are spaced out nicely. She knows a lot about the subject, and will meet with you outside of class if needed. She is easy to talk to and is a fair grader.

analysis.name: Elizabeth Marsch
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: If you do the assigned work ( a lot but manageable) you will do pretty well. The class was all discussion and participation based. Students gave their thoughts on the readings the entire lecture. The midterm and finals were essays (tough grader). There was one presentation about a quote.
Too much work to not learn a lot.

My favorite class and prof at OSU. Tons of discussion. She listens really closely to what students are saying, and it seems like she's just going to let everyone talk, but then she somehow summarizes everything and puts it into an intellectual framework and ties it back into class. She always made my ideas sound smarter than I thought they were.

This teacher notices everything, even when she doesn't say anything. She actually really cares about the students in her class as people. We've had the best conversations in her office. I went there to talk about the exam and we ended up talking about my life. OMG she doesn't accept laziness from people, though, like, at all.

She just exudes love--not creepy, just really inspiring. I'm learning a lot from what she assigns, but also who she is. Perfect for a class on love, which is an impossible topic anyway ("I'm not sure I know much about love, but I know a lot about what other people across the world say about it. Let's look at some and see what we think." Awesome.)

analysis.name: Steve Bibyk
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 76 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Awesome prof.  Study hard and go to class. The students who don't learn anything don't do either of these and just do the minimum to get by (pure laziness.)  Bibyk doesn't spoon-feed but is incredibly helpful towards students who show initiative. After all, we're in college, not high school.

Dr. Bibyk is an awesome professor!  He is difficult (especially regarding the tests) but definitely fair.  He is genuinely interested in helping students understand the material and knows his stuff. He has wealth of knowledge in Digital/Analog VLSI.  I definitely recommend him, just don't be lazy student. Put the time in to learn all th
Waste of my tuition. Did not learn a single thing.

If you are willing to take initiative, his classes are informative and somewhat easy. He provides answers to homework, even tests during lecture, but projects and studying for the final should always be a group effort.

Prof. Bibyk does not lecture like 90% of profs. He simply introduces you to the material and expects you to read/skim the text book and websites and learn the material how ever you can. He does not spoon feed at all. If you take his class and follow what he says to do YOU WILL LEARN SO MUCH.

analysis.name: Tania Burgos Hernandez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Tania is a great professor; it's very clear she wants her students to succeed and get interested in material. There are a lot of assigned readings, but they aren't really discussed in class other than her reteaching the material, so you can easily get away with not reading them unless you're confused. She isn't a very engaging professor, however.

Dr. Tania is awesome. I took the lecture online and the lectures were straight forward, just a little long. Everything is open note and she doesn't use lockdown browser. Some tiny tiny projects here and there but they are so easy and actually interesting. Last project is very very difficult but go to TA office hours and they will be happy to help!

She's so great. I loved her class! I didn't need it for my major (I just took it for upper division credit). But it was really informative and enjoyable. She's clearly so passionate about what she does and it shines through in how she lectures. Highly recommend.
Nothing to write home about. Assignments were easy, though sometimes points were taken off for arbitrary reasons. All in all, easy three credits.

I had ENR 3000 online (would not let me select correct course code) and it was a breeze! I learned a lot even though it was online, and Tania was extremely nice and helpful. Easy to get good grades and much of it is self paced with quick grading and flexible deadlines. Definitely would recommend taking her if possible!

analysis.name: Elizabeth Miller
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She was a very fair grader & as long as you put in the work it is a pretty easy A. She is very nice & accommodating if you don't get something done right on time. Three major projects that are a little time consuming, but the other assignments were not too bad.
I thought I was going to hate 2277 but I absolutely loved it. Would have Prof. Miller again without hesitation even though I'm an engineering student.
Professor Miller is very caring and accommodating. She is a fair grader and wants all the students to do well. She has clear expectations that are easy to follow.

analysis.name: Bradford Findell
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: You have to work hard for this class. Go to office hours or you will not do well. Do the sample problems he gives you, some will appear on the exams. Stay organized or you will regret it. He can be very confusing at times and can talk down to you, but he does care about each of his students and wants the best for us.

This is for MATH 1295 ONLY. Which is the mathematics majors survey course. His lectures were interactive and I enjoyed watching what others put. There is hardly any course work at all. If you get anything lower than an A you just weren't in class. He went through some math topics in unexpected fields such as pharmacokinetics and cartography.

The class time work was very simple and easy, but the midterm did not have much to do with what we learned at all and he graded extremely tough. The final was a take home final and he said it would be graded before the end of the semester, but it was not  and really hurt some people's grades who depended on this final to bring their grade up.

Lectures in this class had nothing to do with what was on the exams. He grades extremely hard on the tests and takes off a ridiculous amount of points for small things. He tells us we are messy, and is disrespectful to all students. Avoid this professor at all costs.

Class was semi-enjoyable and not super difficult, but final grades are completely unreasonable. There are barely any homework assignments in the class, so most of your grade is based on the midterm and take-home final. The take-home final has no clear rubric, and is not similar to what we did in class at all.

analysis.name: Comert Kural
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 77 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I thought Kural was a good professor to give you the baseline knowledge to succeed, but you also need to put in a decent amount of work outside of class. I recommend using the multiple choice problems in his slides and really understanding these underlying concepts the night before an exam/quiz.

Comert's lectures were NOT helpful to me at all. He goes over lecture slides from the book which is helpful but does only a couple example problems and skips over the practice probs way before you even have a chance to look at them. I started doing better on the quizzes when I stopped going to lecture. His test are hard no matter how much you study

He's very good at explaining in lectures and his exams are fairly difficult; however, if you look over practice exams, quizzes, and notes; he takes questions straight from them and tweaks them slightly

No. If you have him for Physics 1201, drop and switch professors. He was so unhelpful and unprofessional when I went to him for help in the course. His quizzes and tests are over questions far more difficult and in depth than those discussed in class. I spent HOURS reviewing the textbook and homework's before each quiz. Good luck, you'll need it.

Most down to earth professor I have ever had. He is hilarious with make the class enjoyable. His explanation is also hilarious which help with understanding the topics. The two midterms were extremely easy. But Final took me by a surprise. So study your butts off for final.

analysis.name: Steven Brown
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 134 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: My favorite teacher so far at Ohio State. He comes into class every day full of energy and coffee in hand. It was the only 8am I would ever take again. He makes possibly dull content entertaining. If you are looking for a fun, easy A class, take this. You will learn a lot about how/why we think the things we do.

Best classroom experience I've had at Ohio State! I came for the credit, I stayed for the captivating lectures, and I left with a new view on the world and the people around me. Steven Brown is simply amazing.

Funny professor! Going to class is an enjoyable experience. Youll learn a lot about the philos as well as random tidbits about the world when he digresses:) Easy A Only 2 midterms which you will be allowed a cheat sheet for. I recommend this class to anyone as long as you do not get offended easily by controversial subjects. He won't sugarcoat

Favorite professor ever. He genuinely cares so much about his students and class discussions. He structures the class in a very discussion/participation-based way, deciding what to talk about based on the class's interests. He's so lively and passionate about his class. Super easy to get an A. Best most entertaining lectures. LOVE him

My favorite professor this year. He was hilarious and passionate about what he was teaching. There's not too much homework besides a few readings and a weekly reflection—but nothing difficult. The exams are 5 FRQs, but he does the notes for you, so you just need to go over those. On the last day of class, he has a tea ceremony with his Grandma.

analysis.name: Casey Saup
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Maybe one of the greatest professors ever, so kind and respectful, sometimes goes a little bit off topic but still finishes in time, the easiest A you might get ever if you just put in an hour of very simple work.
As long as you look over the content deliberately and don't procrastinate, it's impossible to not get an A! The exams have no trick questions and are pretty short ~20 questions. It's so worth it!

The kindest professor I've ever had. The course was only graded on guided notes for the lectures and weekly quizzes (unlimited attempts and time). She was so understanding and aware of student's feelings toward her class and if work load or life just became too much, and would accommodate work/deadlines if needed. Can't recommend her enough.

Honestly one of the best instructors to take, She is very sweet and very caring, puts students mental health before assignments, and overall wonderful person. One of the easiest classes i have ever taken.
So unbelievably easy. Forgot to post material half the time, so barely any work. No midterms, all guided notes and infinite retake quizzes.

analysis.name: Elisabeth Calhoon
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 97 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This class was supposed to be an Introduction to Biology, instead it turned into 15 hour study days for an average grade. The material itself is interesting. However, Dr. Calhoon ruins that. She reads from the slides; this ends up hurting you on the exams, because they are application. Lectures suck. No missed lab policy. Badly structured class.

First off, she makes attendance mandatory even though she records her lectures and reads directly from the slides. Secondly, she never did anything to try to engage people in lecture, so it made it all worse to be forced to attend someone who sounds bored while teaching. Additionally, the grading on lab reports is very harsh for no reason at all.

There's 4 exams, 1 partial cumulative final exam, lots of tophat questions and in class assignments every lecture, assigned seats based on your lab group, so much stuff on the slides, she reads straight from the slides, and the exam questions are worded difficult. The material isn't bad, she just isn't the best. If you study well, you'll be fine.

AVOID HER AT ALL COSTS. She makes General Entry level Bio way harder than it needs to be. Her lectures are painfully boring, but you can't zone out because TopHats count for 10 percent. She has assigned seats, her exam questions are hard for no reason, and if your TA  for lab is a Dr., DROP IMMEDIATELY. I had to retake Bio even with a 4 on AP Bio.

Just a really Boring experience. I didn't pay attention during the lectures at all and really didn't get much out of the lectures. But you have to attend them because of TopHat assignments. The only reason I'm not saying 1 is because the final exam study guild she gave was very helpful and the notes are a good way to prep for tests.

analysis.name: James Chiucchi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Super fun class, makes things enjoyable. Tests are fair but you do have to study for them. He and most of the TAs are very helpful

Dr. Chiucchi was a great lecturer. He really knew his stuff. I felt like I did nothing in the class, but when looking back I learned so much! He does assign papers but they can be pretty easy. The book is not necessary!

Chiucchi was an ok professor. During his lectures, I felt like I knew what he was teaching us. Until those exams came. The questions were so finicky like whaaat? He says he gives straightforward questions but some of them weren't easy. Honestly actually go through the slides. It not an easy A like everyone says it is. Work hard and good luck!

Dr. Chiucchi is a fantastic professor. He really knows the material, and is passionate about it. He is pretty open to questions during lecture, and he uses TopHat to judge class understanding and will elaborate when there are signs of misunderstanding. That being said, don't sign up for 1114.02.
PLTL is useless and will make you want to cry. Do .01

The notes he uses are filled with images with no in text explanation making it hard to relate them to anything for the exams. The content is fairly simple but the exams make it extra confusing and test your ability to read more than knowing the content.

analysis.name: Stephen Chordas
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 162 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: While he may be a nice and funny guy, which I love about him, he does not teach practically at all during lecture. He will go on a story about his life for 20 minutes and then the rest of class is his slideshow that is sloppily put together and is the only study materials in the course. Do not recommend if you actually plan on learning something.

The guy is a nice person, but honestly the teaching is bad. Lectures are mostly just him talking about random stuff instead of actually teaching the material. There are no study guides or helpful resources whatsoever. Literally nothing. the slides are really bad and don't explain anything clearly. avoid at all costs

He lets the class decide how your grade will be made up by a survey in the 1st week. Labs make up a large portion of your grade and tend to drag on week to week. analysis.name: Min Tian
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Min is one of the best professors at Fisher—kind, approachable, and truly invested in students' success. The workload is fair, and she explains material clearly. Grading is detail-oriented, so pay attention. The group project is manageable, and SPSS feels useful by the end. A fair, worthwhile class.
She is one of the kindest professors on campus. She genuinely cares so much for her students!!!!!

BUSML 7252: Awesome personality, obviously loves to teach. Downside, 8 wks of instruction in a 7 wk class w/ work during spring break. Plan to spend more than 3 hrs /wk on this 1.5 c/h course. It was taught w/ R studio, but the proctored exam only allows a calculator(using Proctorio for an elective!?). If your not already statistic savvy, skip.

Do not take this class with Min. Does not explain anything and terrible grader. Seems as if grades are predetermined. No matter how well you do you get the exact same grade on everything. Cannot get above a 91-95% depending on the project, which makes it nearly impossible to get an A and only believes 25% of the class should be able to get an A.

analysis.name: Mary Sterenberg
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class is clearly laid out from the start. There is a lot of work but is very manageable due to the way she prepared it all. There is a group project that occurs throughout the semester with a real client. There were no exams. Also, she provided clear instructions/feedback to assignments and writing pieces. She cares about our success!

I LOVE MARY. She is a semi-strict grader--big stickler on grammar and AP style (no passive voice!), but she encourages you to use AI to screen your assignments for these things. She also doesn't accept late work, but the work is so easy. There are lots of points to pad your grade should you miss a weekly quiz. If you're competent, you'll be fine.

This course does have a lot of work but it is very manageable and laid out clearly. Mary is very personable and professional making her an overall great professor. Everything is organized and there is no surprises. Lots of good experience that you will take with you for interviews and the workforce.

I enjoy this class but it feels like a bad fit for me. Mary seems to love AI and it is used in every class and is even required for some assignments. I would way rather have AI be not allowed. She is super kind and a great listener.

I liked Mary! She seems to really care about her students and she is a fair grader. You just have to follow the rubrics and what she teaches in lecture to get an A. Don't miss class much because there are participation assignments for points that she doesn't let you make up. The online textbook is short and painless to read for the quizzes.

analysis.name: Tawfiq Musah
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Tawfiq is one of the best professors I've had at my time at OSU. He gets to know each of his students quickly, checks on them periodically, and volunteers lots of time outside of class for chances to get help. In addition, his lectures are great and his advice from his time in industry is very helpful and insightful. OSU is very lucky to have him.

Tawfiq is a fantastic professor who is very passionate, engaging, and intelligent. Can come across as intimidating but truly just wants you to learn and apply yourself. He is very caring and willing to help. His wit and charisma made his lectures the best part of my semester.

Class was very difficult for me at least but he puts a strong emphasis on you actually knowing the material. While he does this he does an amazing job at teaching you the material and making sure you really know it.
Originally scared class into thinking it was going to be terribly difficult, but as time went on it got much easier.  Very funny guy that will really force you to learn and not just memorize.
Professor is very overhyped he's fine. I find him to be annoying but other students seem to like him because he engages with students, but how he does it is not very nice or productive.

analysis.name: Michelle McWhorter
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She's really nice and gives really good lectures for content that can be boring at times if it isn't your passion. Her exams were tricky at times, and some exam questions felt like a really niche part of lecture instead of the big picture. However, I enjoyed her passion and it seems like she never got bored of the topic she was speaking on.

She's new at OSU and tends to make small technology/canvas related mistakes. Exams were challenging, but she was responsive to feedback and offered additional credit when averages were low. We were allowed to have a huge notecard on exams. Overall a fair instructor, would recommend.

Lectures were fine but the exams are so hard. Exams test so much more in depth compared to what was mentioned in lecture. It's genuinely insane. Please if you see this Ms. McWhorter, change the exam questions to be easier. I once studied so hard and got below average, after doing everything she recommended (I studied for 8 hours straight)

I loved Mcwhorter. The only thing I will say were that her exams were HARD but please please go over the ungraded problem sets. Also make sure you realize how things connect and you will do okay! . But she wants to help you, so please go to her office hours. She is a good professor! Would take her again.

A very nice and approachable professor. However, her lecture style is confusing and boring, and I found that the slide content is too simple for what is actually being tested. The ungraded HW she uses as exam practice is unhelpful because new material is tested that isn't discussed in lectures. I would not take this class with her again.

analysis.name: Naomi Zweben
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
I've had the pleasure of having Dr. Zweben for Software 1 and I can confirm that everything said about her here is 100% true.

She gives extra credit often and is very understanding of circumstances. She usually has a 12:40-1:35 section so take that if you want to get her for the 2024 spring semester. 

Makes CSE 2221 1000x easier.

Dr. Zweben is super understanding and communicates the content well. She takes students' needs into consideration and recognizes that we have a life outside of class, which from my understanding is not common in the CSE department. I had her for CSE 1223 as well and I think I got a very good understanding of Java and coding practices from her.

This class is a weed out class, but she does everything to make sure it doesn't feel that way. She uses a lot of advanced vocab in her lectures which can make it hard to keep up, but she genuinely cares about her students and offers help with open arms. She created her own exams which were aligned perfectly with what was learned in class. Love her!

Naomi cares a lot about student success and does a great job breaking down difficult material in SW1. She provides copious review opportunities and is very approachable when students ask questions. The course feels fast paced, so it requires consistent effort, but the support she provides makes a big difference. I would totally recommend her.

genuinely the model of what a prof/lecturer should be. explains concepts very well, accessible outside of class, very approachable for questions. also posts video recordings for lectures. software 1 is an intimidating class but she makes it feel easy. hw assignments/exams are all very fair and she prepares you well.

analysis.name: Nickalaus Painter
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 68 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: There's nothing to complain about with painter. He has a great understanding of the students' perspective and clearly wants others to succeed. Painter makes a great effort to be clear and specific with his lectures, and never makes things unnecessarily complicated. He is also pretty funny, and very relatable. (glaze warranted + i'm heterosexual)

No joke, this guy rocks. With Mr. Painter, it's less like being a pupil than it is working with a teammate to solve a problem. Teaching style is very unique and seemingly universal (I know it is not just me- I've read the reviews). Classroom setting welcomes openness and collaboration. Prepare to learn a lot without realizing you are even working.

Dr. Painter is one of the most caring professors and understands students have other commitments. There is homework/reflections daily and they are time consuming but nothing too difficult. You do have to study well for exams, as this is still DSA. Grades leniently on HW but more harsh on exams. However, he is easily the best prof for this course

HIGHLY recommend taking Painter for 2331. Straightforward class. Attendance not required. There is homework for each lecture but they are quick, easy and mostly graded for effort. He has great youtube lectures that show exactly how to do everything. Notes/studying not needed. Exams are comically easy; you really have to try not to get an A.

Optional attendance which is nice because you can watch the videos online on your time. The class had a lot of homework and reflections on the homework. The exams were fair and questions based on the homework but still required studying to do well. Good class overall.

analysis.name: Neil DeBoer
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 61 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Calc 2 is a difficult class no matter who you end up having as a professor. I believe Neil did a very good job in his lectures in explaining concepts and always answered questions whenever people had them. In calc 2 specifically, I see no reason for him to be a 1-star as anything unrelated to lecturing is dependent on the math department.

The most boring class you will ever take, he will kill all of your motivation to try and learn the content and will get you into a habit of skipping class so that you dont have to hear his quiet warble of a lecture.

The math department needs to be fixed for this class. He releases no lecture notes, writes on a chalkboard, and talks monotone the entire time. His examples are not helpful at all in terms of comprehension and exams are harder than any work you will do for homework or in lecture. You will need a tutor and to learn everything yourself.

Honestly if i had to choose between retaking this class or fighting thanos, i would choose the thanos every single time. First of all, you have to teach yourself for majority of the time because he does not do a good job at all when it comes to making sure people are learning what they're supposed to learn. Recitation was the biggest joke

Let me start by saying he's a really nice and misunderstood guy that is very knowledgeable. With that being said, his lectures are very monotone and the recitation was abysmal. I stopped going to lecture and recitation halfway through the semester and self-studied to get an A. I don't recommend at all, but is doable if it's a last resort.

analysis.name: Nima Safaei
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Nima is an excellent professor who genuinely cares about his students and explains the material clearly. He's flexible with deadlines and responds to emails quickly. With that said, the course is taught as part of a master class and graders are tough though!

Sitting in his class as we speak, currently showing us the same table on the board and from two different tabs on his computer on the projector. Just spent 40 minutes filling in an indifference table. I don't know if I can do this anymore. 

Seems like a nice guy tho no hate.
Seems like a nice guy but his lectures might be the most boring thing I have ever had to sit through.

analysis.name: Prerna Nadathur
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Excellent professor. The lectures are very clear, and the progression of ideas is easy to follow. The board work is very neat and organized. The homework is challenging and really makes you think. There were 7–8 assignments in total, and I usually spent about 5–6 hours on each one. Learned a lot from this class!

Well rounded, all-around great class. Lectures are super important (and interesting), so go to them. A good amount of homework, but you can work with your peers, which is nice. Ask questions and engage, it'll make the class much more interesting. I found it to be easy, but some peers found it challenging; perspective on difficulty will vary.

analysis.name: Nick Breyfogle
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: You can tell he cares so much about the subject, and this class is very interesting. However, it is SO much reading nearly every week, with the occasional hour long lecture posted to be watched outside of class. Just a lot of reading and effort expected overall.
His lectures are very engaging. It's clear he cares a lot about the topic. There is a lot of reading, but not an overwhelming amount.

Good dude, he makes it a really interesting class. The papers are hard and its graded really tough but you can get up to 10% of extra credit and the discussion section of the class is worth 30% of your grade so if you read and participate you'll get a good grade even if you don't do too hot on the papers.

Easily one of the best professors I've ever had. His lectures are very interesting and well organized and his sense of humor is great. He's always more than happy to talk after class too. He is a bit of a tough grader and the tests aren't exactly easy. You'll have a ton of reading too and if you don't do it you're screwed. I give this class 8.5/10

Professor Breyfogle was my favorite professor and I found a new interest in European history because of his enthusiastic lectures. He makes the class exciting and he is interested in the material. Study guides are terms that will be selected from for the tests, preparation is all you need for an A. Would HIGHLY recommend. Attendance is important

analysis.name: Jennifer Ottesen
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I was so interested in biochem when we started. After taking her, my interest in biochem went down a lot. It's not even the material. It's just the way she teaches. She will talk about stuff in class that isn't even on the exam. Also, her exams are very vague on what to write. Majors can't avoid taking her because she's the only one who teaches it.

My only regret of freshman year was choosing to take this course. The lab assignments took hours, we often got entire lectures behind, and she was not very friendly when approached for help during office hours. I studied weeks in advance for her exams and still never got above a 78. Any regular bio 1113 class is easier, no matter the professor.

Dr. Ottesen should not be allowed to teach this level of biology. She was unable to effectively communicate a majority of the material, and her lectures left me feeling extremely confused. She frequently went off on unrelated tangents that put us behind. She was not approachable for help and often passive aggressive. This class ruined my semester.

I really struggled in this class, and have fought tooth-and-nail for my grade. Dr Ottesen is extremely mediocre at her job. Quite frankly, as someone who came from a poor area with no APs, I struggled. She expected everyone to have known all of Chem 1 basically, and her portion of the course was basically Biochem 1. Avoid this class for your sake.

Took AP Bio in HS and got a 5. This class is a lot harder, not because it only goes deeper into the material, but Dr. Ottesen teaches it like we are graduate students to some extent, and the lectures are not very helpful. Just take the normal one and save urself the time and effort. Dr. Ottesen is a nice person, but she is not good for beginners.

analysis.name: Christopher O’Daniel
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Honestly the worst professor I have ever had. All of his in class examples are pre-filled in before class, and all he does is unhighlight them. Worst of all most of them are the incorrect answer and you are solving the problem yourself. He also isn't engaging at all. You are teaching yourself everything in this class. Exams are very hard too.

He is the most boring professor I have ever had.  Basically your only grades are exams.  There are 4 quizzes and a final, but the quizzes are 50 questions on lockdown, with a 60 minute time limit.  This class is basically and exam every other week. 

Would never take him again. I am honestly surprised he is still employed by OSU. Must have tenure.

genuinely never had a worse professor than this guy. For a class where the content really is not that difficult, your gpa gets messed up because this guy pulls the most random stuff out on the exam that even if it was covered in lecture there is no way you would have even caught it because he was the most boring professor i have ever had.

Extremely nice guy but not a great teacher. Nobody goes to lecture because you don't really get anything useful out of it in terms of exam prep. At least attendance was not mandatory. The exams are extremely difficult, but each one has a small weight as there are four total which helps if you really mess one up.

You couldn't pay me to sit through one of his classes again.  He is the most boring and worst teacher I have ever had.  You basically have an exam every 2-3 weeks with almost no other grades. Genuinely have no clue how he has a job at OSU.  DO NOT TAKE HIM.

analysis.name: Alexis Ortiz-Rosario
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. OR is very nice and helpful during the labs when we have lots of questions. He responds to emails pretty quickly and is always respectful. He takes attendance at lectures and lab attendance is mandatory. Overall I would definitely take this course with him again, and it was pretty easy.

Tons of people in class were clearly cheating in groups and the professor did nothing about it. Tough to get responses from him on emails with questions about homework. In person, the TA was better at answering questions than the professor. Easier version of ME2850 but a very forgettable class.

Strange guy but decent professor and kind, clearly cares about BME. He wasn't neglectful but clearly didn't really bother to fix assignments from previous semesters. Literally just half try and you'll get an A. He made it interesting for what it was (MATLAB, gross).
Rude and condescending in office hours, constantly late to class and kind of awkward to talk to.

analysis.name: Olga Kamenchuk
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She doesn't know how to teach. don't take it

so when i read all of these reviews, i thought i was screwed for the class. honestly, you don't need to pay attention in class (you can just cram the night before) and not even have the textbook (paid $350 for it and never ONCE opened it) because you can just make flashcards based off her lecture notes. yes, it's super boring, but not difficult!

I was freaked out when I read the comment about her. I am glad that I didn't drop her class. I've been taking two classes with her, and the structure is the same. 4 exams (drop 1), watch documentaries, papers, EC. She gives detailed study guides for the exams. There are also simple class practices where you need to attend for participation points.

Olga is pretty nice and shares lots of industry anecdotes, but her lectures are slow and not at all engaging. It makes it difficult to be successful in her exams, because you must carve out a lot of time to study the volume of content (since you are not learning in lecture). I have now taken two classes with Olga, and both were mediocre at best.

Attendance is mandatory, lectures are long, tedious, and EXTREMELY dry. Nobody pays attention because she is not engaging at all. You have to reteach yourself the material before the exam, she asks very specific questions about her lecture examples, and her slides are bullet points that her and her husband share. Shouldn't be a professor.

analysis.name: Daniel Olson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Glacial response to emails. Had to literally get his boss involved so he'd get off the PlayStation and do his job. Otherwise not too bad - boring, honestly.

Straight forward expectations from the get-go. Readings due before pretty much every class (20-30 pages per class period). Assignments self-paced, not many outside of participation (if so, mainly papers). He's passionate in class and at office hours. Flexible with due dates. A little socially awkward at times. Good vibes overall.
Very clear what was expected, had a reading before every class but was very manageable. 4 papers throughout the term, took AU 24.

Amazing professor. Gives very clear lectures and he explains the content in a way where you understand. He is very clear on the grading material. Exams are super easy if you showed up to class and did the readings, there are no surprises or tricks questions. DEFINITELY TAKE HIM!!! Attendance is mandatory so if you want that A show up and try.
Very slow at responding to emails.

analysis.name: Osei Appiah
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Attending class is a WASTE OF TIME. The midterms are a guessing game because he DOES NOT TEACH. He only talks about his family and basketball. I can tell he's a nice guy, but not a good teacher at all.

Seems like a fun dude to talk ball with, but did not enjoy his class. Lots of difficult reading for homework and long, boring video lectures. You do get to watch Skip and Shannon or other sports documentaries for extra credit which is a plus

Where do I even start, first of all these people do not know how to rate a professor. Whatever you do, DO NOT TAKE HIM FOR ANY OF THE COMM CLASSES. Unorganized, exams are a guessing game, did not teach just talked about his son and basketball, rude, doesn't communicate… I could go on. TA was helpful but professor doesn't communicate clearly to him.

Prof is funny and a good guy but his class was incredibly unorganized, grade is based off of 3 midterms, which were a bit of a guessing game, and a group project that was also not well organized. Could tell him and the TA rarely communicated with another. Lecture heavy, and he goes on random tangents. Never bought the book tho, and ended with a B+

This professor is interesting. But this class makes students so confused. After the second midterm, the entire class is based on guest speaker (they are on zoom) and group presentation. He asked us to come to class, but nothing is worth learning in class. The professor not willing to teach, and the TA does not communicate well with the professor.

analysis.name: Tracy Owens
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I loved Professor Owen's class. He is down-to-earth and understands what's important to the students. He is very flexible and offers many out-of-class opportunities for research experiences. The class itself was fun, besides it being an evening class. Open-book, open-note exams. He genuinely cares.

Tracy is by far the best professor at Ohio State. At least in the ISE department. He genuinely cares about each student and strives to make sure everyone is comfortable in his class. Could not speak more highly of him!

Tracy Owens is easily the best professor at Ohio State. Just learning from him is worth the extra work of the L&SS capstone program. He cares about each student individually, will match the effort you put in, and goes above & beyond to apply any feedback he is given! I can't speak highly enough of him.

If you can take this course with Professor Owens, do yourself the favor and do it! Tracy balances being hands-off while also walking with you through this course well. He trusted my group's judgment on decisions, but was always willing to help if need be. The experience gained through this course is priceless. Easy choice to get your green belt!

Best professor I've had at OSU! Can definitely tell how much he cares about Six Sigma and genuinely wants to help each student pass the Green Belt certification class. Definitely have to put in the work outside of class and pay attention during, but it is so worth it

analysis.name: Parisa Roustazadeh
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Do everything you can to not take this professor. You can 100% skip the lecture; it's at an elementary level, but you get slammed on quizzes and the midterm. Make sure you understand the physics concepts, as the questions are poorly written and many of the tests ? are completely new, and she deliberately doesn't identify any patterns.

She is nice and means well, but is not great at teaching. The recitations will teach and explain concepts better than she does. Exams are multiple choice and can be difficult, but there is always a big curve. I never took physics before this, so this class was hard for me. But if you put in effort to learn the material, you should be okay.

Her lectures are extremely hard to understand. She teaches the material very briefly like you already know it. Her slides are unorganized. Tests are very difficult, multiple choice, 15 questions, 6 pts each, no partial credit. Almost everyone fails them, they're curved to a 77%.  I switched lecturers after 3 weeks. Do not recommend.

Respectfully, the worst professor I've had. She does not know how to teach, which is unfortunate. You'll realize by week 3 that lectures are entirely useless. The sooner you quit her lectures and switch to YouTube, the better off you will be. Her saving grace is that, because her scores are lower than other profs, there are a LOT of bonus points.

Dr. R is one of the worst professors I've had. Bc you are a course coordinator, does not mean you can be a prof. I didn't take physics in high school, & this was a hard course for me. She goes over 30+ slides with heavy info in a short time. She's so educated in physics, she doesn't know how to teach students who are starting from the ground up.

analysis.name: Paul Martini
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: You can tell Dr. Martini really enjoys teaching his students. He really likes talking about the different astronomy topics and that makes the class fun to be in. He sometimes would go on some tangents but they were not often and wouldn't last for very long.

He's SOO CUte like a little teddy bear. But seriously, this class was really interesting. The lectures were engaging and very cool. Grades are based mainly on four quizzes+final, which you probably will end up studying a solid amount for. Definitely not the easiest class ever (there were lessons that were pretty challenging), but still worth it imo

He is one of the nicest prof's I've ever had at OSU. He is really helpful if you go to his office hours. You can tell how passionate he is on the subject. He gives multiple choice questions during the lecture (not for a grade) to make sure we understand everything, it's a good checkpoint. He takes attendance sometimes. Study hard but it's worth it

By far the hardest class I've taken in college, and I'm a junior. Completely unfair that this class is a GEC. You have a 50 point quiz every other Friday and then a cumulative final, as well as 4 homeworks which are purposefully harder than the material learned. Lectures are dry and hard to pay attention to, and you cover a new chapter everyday.

if you have any basic interest in astronomy at all, he will make this an easy and interesting class for you. he's very clear, very helpful, and very interesting. it was an easy A for me and my buddies, and a perfect GEC. plus he tells jokes that are so bad they're good. highly recommended.

analysis.name: Clay Partridge
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS W/ CLAY. Also any time we have a quiz or something and the average was good he will say he made it too easy and needs to make it harder he does not care about us getting a good grade.

Clay is a good guy with a lot of accounting experience. However, it's very difficult to study for his exams because he asks questions almost completely different than anything in his notes or homeworks. The goal for him is for us to be able to apply the concepts to many situations, but the resources he gives don't help at all. I recommend avoiding

I'm sorry but Professor Partridge is the absolute worst professor I've ever had at Ohio State. He goes extremely fast in lecture, doesn't provide hardly any extra practice, and his exams are unreasonably difficult. I would do everything in my power to take this class with literally any other professor. Save yourself now!

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH PARTRIDGE. He doesn't give any exam review material, doesn't post any of his notes or lectures from class, and is not engaging at all. Do everything in your power to take this class with a different professor. One bad test and your grade is done for.

Do NOT take this professor. His exams are so hard and the averages are like Ds. His lectures are often confusing and he contradicts himself so many times. He's a weird teacher overall who thinks that going over exams are unnecessary. I learned more from the textbook than from him. (the textbook is optional but it saved my grade on the last exam)

analysis.name: Jon Quinn

review_highlights.comment: Professor Quinn is a fantastic professor. He is a very engaging lecturer, and participation matters a lot in class discussion. You definitely have to put in the work, and the exams are hard, but it is a great class. I wish I could have taken another class with him during my last semester as he is one of my favorite professors at Fisher.

Quinn has been one of my favorite lecturers in Fisher. The first test caught me off guard, so definitely study everything he gives you, as it's more so memorizing the terms than common sense. Every other assignment is an easy A+. He makes his lecture's super interesting too. Class is a very easy B and an attainable A with some effort.
great professor, had him for multiple classes and i love his lectures. exams are hard but the class is pretty easy otherwise. super engaging and funny in class

Quinn might be a nice guy, but this class is brutal. Exams average a 65 with no curve, and on top of a 1.5-hour lecture, there's 1–2 extra hours of asynchronous content weekly. It feels like a full-time job. Unless you love pain, avoid if possible.
Professor Quinn is truly the best. His class is very straight forward and he really lays out the concepts well. He is a great guy and will work with you through whatever you are struggling with!!!

analysis.name: Rongjun Qin
