Ridiculous turnaround time on grades. 4-6 weeks to get grades back on papers. No responses to emails. Vague instructions with no clarification.

analysis.name: Valentin Kunz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Valentin is an awesome professor, he is funny and cares about student success but sometimes teaches as if we already know the material. Personally I learned more from my recitation/TA but his lectures were still helpful. The math department doesn't try to screw you over, the midterms/quizzes are very similar to the practice ones. No cheat sheets.

Although I think his resources are great, such as test and exam reviews, he moves wayy too fast in lecture and kind of already expects you to have some base knowledge on the topic he discusses. other than that, he's a great professor and you can tell he wants everyone to move on to the next step, adorable and great professor overall.

Professor Kunz likes to heavily teach theory in a math class with all engineers who do not want theory taught to them. His lectures are very hard to follow and understand. His writing is hard to understand. He makes simple topics extremely complicated. I will say his exams were easy, exactly like the practice exams he gives us to study for.

Kunz was a very good professor and was always easy to reach. Getting used to his writing was a little difficult but doable. My main concern with this class was his lectures. Lectures were pretty theory heavy, and extremely fast paced. If you take this class make sure to remind him slow down and go through full problems without skipping steps.

Grind out recitations, as the TAs are typically able to slow things a lot as opposed to Valentin during the lecture. However, Valentin's notes are quite a great resource to review come exam time. Exams are not particularly tricky, and quizzes are just like the practices.

analysis.name: Aimee Ulstad
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The class is boring but fairly easy as long as you understand how to do the problems. Textbook is not necessary but you have to buy homework access. She is a decent professor and explains the material clearly. Exams are not very many questions so any question you miss will impact your grade significantly so be aware of that.

Aimee is an awesome professor. She does a great job of explaining the course material rather than just regurgitating it. She also gives you a chance to miss a few classes by putting her lectures online and dropping a fair amount of quizzes you take every day in class.
Very clear and always willing to help with the material. The 4 hour lectures can drag on and become very boring though as she goes through example problems at a slow pace.
Easy class, come to lectures, study example problems and it's an easy AB+. Lectures are long but I heard that's changing to hour lectures so it should be a good class

The course is short but the lectures can be boring. Purchasing homework access is forced but save yourself the money and don't bother with the textbook, it's not helpful in anyway. Forces you to do clicker questions from a phone app at random points during random lectures. The course isn't hard, just tedious.

analysis.name: Linda Villarreal
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
She is top of the line, nothing less! Even if it was a Spanish course, it was something to look forward to. She's engaging, entertaining, and often funny.

Coursework is challenging, but enough to feel rewarded about it, not exhausted. Show up to class, raise your hand a little, and you're golden!

11/10. I hope to have her again!

Linda has been one of my favorite professors by far. Keep in mind this is a 1101+1102 class combined, so the work load will not be as light as it would be if you took a single level. However, she always makes the subject as simple as possible. Very nice grader, and participation is a must. TAKE THIS PROF IF YOU WANT A GREAT FOREIGN LANG EXPERIENCE!

I cannot speak more highly of this professor. She was kind and understanding to work with and completely changed the way I approach my Spanish classes. Since 1155 combines two classes, there is a lot of material, but the homework was manageable and consistent each week. I definitely recommend her.

In my past, I've never really liked spanish due to some poor professors ive had in the class, but profe made spanish for me fun again. If you just do the work and it will be an easy A. She's very nice and caring and sent a great email to the whole class about her appreciation.

Prof. Linda is the best Spanish prof I've ever had. I couldn't imagine taking this tough course without her—she made it fun and easy to learn. After a bad 1103 experience, I almost gave up on my minor, but she reignited my love for Spanish and always encouraged me!

analysis.name: Vince Castillo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Castillo is a great guy. Really cares about the material he teaches. Such a valuable class that also touches on using/understanding AI. This class continues to keep me interested and wanting to learn more about demand planning and AI. The use of coding and RStudio is something that could be very beneficial down the road too... 10/10 class

Not a good professor teaches material that is unneeded for jobs after graduating. Races through powerpoint slides during class and especially on lab days. Overall I would not take him again. Really bad teacher avoid at all costs.

Probably one of my favorite Professors. He cares about the material he teaches, and you learn applicable material and programs that you can apply in Logistics. I highly recommend his course. Only advise I'd give to others is to brush up on stats, because a lot of the material will make more sense if you do.

analysis.name: Vincent Vu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Homework was difficult, and the video lectures often didn't provide enough information to answer some of the questions. Takes off lots of points if formatting isn't perfect on homework documents.

Vu gives clear lectures and replies to emails quickly. He is sometimes a bit sassy/intimidating one-on-one, but it's coming from a good place. His exams are difficult but fair, and the HWs are reasonable. His occasionally super shiny head can be distracting during lectures - aside from that, he's much better than I expected.

Awesome professor who explains the concepts clearly. He runs the class in an efficient and high quality manner. However, he grades the exams very harshly and requires precise answers (but it is curved). Overall, a great professor who I would recommend!
Vince was a good lecturer, however, his tests were very difficult and he graded quite harshly. The midterm averages always hovered around 50% or 60%.

Vince is a organized teacher, but there were some problems. Firstly, whenever me or people ask for help in the discussion board, Vince would usually say "DId YoU nOT seE the LEcTure VideO?". I did see the lecture and readings and thats why I am asking for help in the first place. Secondly, the homework can be really challenging and really long...

analysis.name: Amit Vutha
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 119 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: He is probably the most dedicated math prof at OSU. He is very easy to approach and made a hard class like Math 1172 doable. He is very knowledgeable and interested in what he does. Honestly he helped me change the way I look at math.

Amit is one of the best math professors I have ever had, always willing to help and arrange office hours to help you, it was 1172 so it is NOT an easy class by any means but his teaching is wonderful and he is a great guy.

Prof Vutha is the reason I did well in this class. He was always available to meet if you sent him an e-mail, even outside of his regular office hours. His exam reviews were thorough and clear, and he was genuinely interested in helping us understand the material. I remember before the final he held an open study session that went until 2am.

I took Amit's Dynamical Systems and Chaos theory class in Autumn 25. Easily one of the most fascinating courses I've taken. The whole semester builds toward the mathematics behind chaos in the final lecture. Amit explains deep ideas with clarity, and the MATLAB projects + team quizzes really made the class an excellent applied math experience.

This guy is absolutely amazing. I wasn't even in his class, but Vutha subbed in once and I loved him so I attended his office hours. He treated me like a son. He spent hours upon hours tutoring me before every exam. One night, he opened up the math building and sat with us from 9PM-5AM to study for an exam.  Quality human being.

analysis.name: KT Vandergriff
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 57 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: i cannot emphasize how badly people need to avoid this prof. she can't explain any concept properly, will only do one example of a topic, and move on quickly. my notes don't even make sense when i write everything down. projects are very difficult. overall AWFUL!

Only 50% of students passed her class last semester.  Assumes every single student has an extensive background in coding. No chance to pass if you don't, and even if you do, like myself, you will struggle. Avoid at all costs.

Tests are way too hard and don't go over what you learn in the slides. She is a nice person, but an extremely difficult professor. Some of my friends in other classes got much easier and fairer tests, don't take her class. Probably half or more of my class failed.

The exams are very difficult and the midterm is only out of 50,  meaning that one wrong multiple choice question (out of 2) turns your midterm grade into a 96%, whereas the other professors' are much more fair and reasonable. Her classes do little to nothing, you need to study on your own. If you want to get a low grade, take her class

she's a nice person but i don't recommend her class. she expects you to have extensive prior knowledge (beyond what's taught in the prereqs) and the exams are harshly graded with questions that are purposefully tricky/confusing.

analysis.name: Vincent Sabino
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The GOAT. Awesome professor who knows AND cares a lot about what he teaches. Class was both educational and fun. Take him if you can!

Sabina is an awesome professor. I learned so much from his class and he really cares about the subjects. As long as you follow directions and do the homework, he grades pretty easily. I am taking a second class with him and I would suggest him to anyone who really wants to learn something.
So finicky. Craft your every discussion post meticulously and make them half-page long or you will lose point! Vague directions and you have no idea why he is grading stuff that way. One word, picky.
Professor Sabino is an amazing instructor. If you show up to class and participate in his class you will be good. He is not a bad grader just put in the work and you will pass the class just fine.

analysis.name: Maggie Wetzel
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Wetzel taught the second half of class and ran the lab portion of this class. She frequently did not know what she was talking about and would be confused during lecture, making everyone teach themselves before the exams. I would not recommend taking her unless she is the only option. Be prepared to study a lot on your own!!!!

Her lectures are sub-par compared to Dr. B's. She seems extremely nervous and just reads off the slides. I find it unnecessary to attend her lectures, I just get the same thing from the slides. She breezes through information and then expects everyone to understand challenging questions immediately. Not a fan.
Don't love her lectures, she kind of jumps all over the place. You're better off learning the material on your own. The exams are harder than anticipated so prepare well.

Lectures really hard to understand. Didn't make sense and topics skipped around a lot. Came out of lectures more confused than when I went in, even with previous knowledge of the topics. Exams were extremely difficult even with studying key topics provided. Material itself is interesting & easy, professor makes it hard to learn. Wouldn't recommend.

Dr. B taught the first half of the class very well and was a great professor. However, Dr. Wetzel was not good at teaching. She was always very nervous during lecture, and just read off the slides. She was not good at explaining concepts or making exams. Please do not take this class with Maggie Wetzel.

analysis.name: Zhiguo Xie
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Xie is very nice, engaging, sometimes humorous. He is willing to share his own personal experience in relation to Chinese culture. Attendance is taken every class,  but he is generous in other grading and gives a lot of bonus opportunities. I feel I learned quite a lot about things I did not know or understand.

This class covered many topics in traditional Chinese culture. Professor delivered the lectures very well. He gave out plenty of bonus opportunities toward the end of the semester. But his frequent cold calling in class sometimes created an anxious atmosphere. Easy A for me.
He very focus your attendance.
Class was super easy. Sometimes interesting, sometimes boring. Mid-term is open book and notes. No final. I don't speak any Chinese and I easily got an A in the course.

Xie laoshi is a great lecturer. He's funny, takes questions/comments well and makes you feel smart every time you talk. Class is long but he makes it enjoyable. Biggest thing is to do the readings, because the quizzes are rough and will hit your grade hard. Very fair on all other assignments. Lectures don't cover the readings, you have to know both

analysis.name: Vladimir Kogan
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 62 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This class is not THAT difficult if you put the time in. You have to go to every class, there are daily reading quizzes. The reading quizzes aren't that hard, they're just tedious. But 50% of your grade is condensed in the last two weeks: group debate, ten page legal brief, take home questions for the final, & the final. Overwhelming in the end.

Very organized, which can't be said of a lot of professors. Have to read because of daily quizzes and participation on Top Hat. Midterm and Final are take-home and not graded harshly. Debate and legal brief at the end are a bit overhwhelming. If you go to class and ready, you should do well with him. Good class for those thinking about law school.

Vlad is honestly a really good professor. One of the POLISCI profs that you can't tell off bat political standings (more right). Guest speakers were pretty ehn. Take home exams take up HOURSSSS. very time consuming and TAs grade them. pretty accessible. participation gives EC so either that or office hours will help buffer grade. MC exams cake.

This class is not hard, it's just time consuming. The only difficult part is the written midterm & final, which took me about a full 3 days to complete each. The grade criteria is very clear, it's just so many parts and a lot of combing thru long readings to complete. The MCQ is incredibly easy, the debate was brownie pts, and quizzes were simple.

If you want to talk about voting and gerrymandering for 16 weeks take this class Take home exams are incredibly time-consuming and difficult. Attendance is not mandatory but you lose so many participation points if you don't go, so you have too. He's a nice guy i guess but wouldn't take his classes again

analysis.name: Xueru Zhang
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is extremely smart, but not very good at conveying the content. The course was laid out and structured well. I think she must be new at teaching because she would get flustered at times when a student would ask a question. Her accent is also extremely strong and created a barrier to understanding.
Great prof, cares about her students, and puts emphasis on learning over memorization. Would take again!

New at teaching. She has good intention and wants everyone to learn but sometimes the way she taught wasn't very clear. Very accessible outside class and willing to help. Large curve, helpful review session and could bring many cheat sheets to exam. Remember to really review your linear algebra and probability before any AI courses.

analysis.name: Xinmiao Zhang
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This is the worst lecturer in the history of school!!!! I dont know what she is saying 99% of the time. Im sitting here crying because I dont know any material for the final since this professor hasnt helped us one bit. No office hours (always cancels), never responds to emails, shame on you ECE dept! Shame on you! RIP my GPA.

I should be studying for this class's final, but here I am rating this class. I didn't learn a thing form her, and probably going to get D in otherwise easy class. She is not interested in helping students, and is hard to follow. She is not fit to teach, and rating of 1 is me being generous, since I cannot rate her 0 here.

All I have to say is, really Ohio State? Don't bother going to class and If you take the class online, don't bother watching the online videos. Everything I learned was straight from the textbook, and her lectures pretty much are a text-to-speech of the text. Not to mention the lectures don't line up the homework. Bring back Mac Ohio State, pls.

She was not the best professor, although some students here are harsh. The exams were somewhat fair, although I feel as if most of the content was only briefly brushed over after the first midterm and not explained in detail. You need to refer to the textbook (which is not good either) to do homework and to supplement learning.

The low reviews from other students seem to be from very long ago, but she is an amazing professor! Her lectures are very clear and insightful, and she doesn't hesitate to reexplain certain concepts to ensure everyone understands them. Lectures are recorded and posted online alongside her notes. Lectures prepare you well for the exams!

analysis.name: Xinyu Liu
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor is a great guy, who genuinely cares about the students. He showed he respected the effort we put in. His lectures were useful but very text and slides heavy, and he can be hard to understand at times. Exams were very hard and all conceptual until the final, but he gave us chances to prove we learned from our mistakes and get points back.

Professor Liu is a wonderful professor to have--he takes great interest in his teaching. He responds to emails almost immediately and answers questions very well. The Midterms and Final are worth a combined 90% toward the final grade, but he curves them extensively. Beware of conceptual questions, which occupy the majority of the exams!

The professor is a good person, but his teaching style is not good. He uses slides to teach mathematics, which feels like memorising rather than understanding. His midterms contain concept questions only; no mathematical questions at all. Everyone in the class did horrendously, and he had to do a curve, which is not a rule for this course.

He's not a bad person and his lectures aren't that bad, but his midterms (worth 20% of our grade each) are completely multiple choice and true/false. The high on our midterm was a B and the median was an F because of trick questions. If you need a high GPA for a scholarship, switch profs ASAP because the HW does not prep you for the exam.

Professor is very nice in person and cares about student's success, but midterms and final are impossible and worth 90% of the grade. The questions are all conceptual so no partial credit and very easy to get low grades.

analysis.name: Xiaodong Zhang
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Zhang is a passionate and proficient Professor who is fair and thorough with grading and teaching. The class content is difficult, but his lectures are highly informative. Lecture is intimidating at first but he only calls on students who raise their hand, so there's nothing to fear. One critique is sometimes his questions in class are unclear.

NOT AN EASY A! but felt very fair - exams were very similar to the homework and during office hours+on piazza he basically walks through hw/exam questions if you ask. have an open mind - comes off as really intimidating at first but he cares about his students and puts in the effort towards being a good teacher, it just looks diff from other profs

He is brilliant in his field, having won numerous awards. However, his teaching style often leaves people struggling. He primarily reads from the slides and says not to memorize much, yet you're expected to know everything on them. It's an exam-heavy class, and the grading is very strict.

Makes an already boring and tough subject unnecessarily worse. Tough grader who insists on students memorizing specific things he reads straight from the slides but maintains that tests are "basic concepts only" and "no memorization." Simply another professor who is not capable of teaching his knowledge.

As someone who took this class after reading this page, I was terrified. I don't feel that the grade accurately reflects his teaching, but more so the 3421 content itself. He tries his best to make all of the content inside of computer architecture as accessible as possible and does his best to give real world examples. Office hours help a lot!

analysis.name: Xiang Li
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Li is amazing for Diff EQ. She's very patient, answers q's simply & makes effort to remember everyone's name. Homework's are simple as are the exams (closely relate).Notes are very easy to follow & will slow down if the class does not understand. Strongly recommend office hours if stuck, she walks through an entire problem if you need it.

I had Professor Li for 2177 but its not here but she is genuinely the best professor Ive had her lectures are very organized and she explains topics really well and if you dont understand her topics she is willing to help after class. Her exams are also very similar to homework problems which makes it easier and just all around a great professor
Organized notes that are easy to understand, useful midterm reviews, always replies her emails and homeworks are similar to her exams. Super nice person overall! (gave us candy for halloween too)

She is extremely kind and always explains topics clearly. The exams match pretty much exactly what was done in class and arguably easier than the homeworks, so as long as you put some work in you'll get a good grade. She is honestly the best math professor at OSU that I have taken so far and I highly recommend her.

Dr. Li is incredibly knowledgeable and patient with students. The grade is based on weekly homework, 3 midterm exams, and a final exam, and she always reviews before exams. She explains the material well and genuinely cares about students' understanding. She also answers emails quickly and extends office hours. Amazing professor for Diff Eq!

analysis.name: Xiaoyan Deng
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Terrible. Tests had typos. Lectures were boringgg. Did not care abt you at all. Exams were outdated. All group based and unreliable. No feedback. Do not take.

Very nice professor! For the most part does a great job teaching. There is a decent amount of reading that is needed outside of class, as this content will be on the exams. Content is also quite interesting. 

Good class and good professor.

This professor is terrible. If you have the option, take someone else. She does not explain anything clearly and will send an e-mail to you the day before a presentation is due  to tell you that you have a presentation to do! The class has potential to be VERY interesting, but she rips that away from the subject completely.

Dr. Deng is great.  You have 5 assignments that account for half of your grade, and she is a very fair and lenient grader on them as long as you put in the effort.  Attendance is not mandatory, but if you go to class it will pay off in the end.  Exams are a little tough, but study the notes (no need for text) and you will be fine. Take Her!
Professor Deng is super nice. The group papers and projects are really easy if you have a good group. Her exams are long but not that difficult, I would suggest to take her for consumer behavior.

analysis.name: Xinyi Ren
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Ren's class is terminology heavy. Exams are somewhat hard but the review sessions helped.
Hands down one of the best professors I've had at OSU. Participation counts but she's fair.

Dr. Ren really cares about her students. If you have any questions, you can just send her a message, and she'll schedule a meeting to help you. Some group projects, but not too much work to do if you're in a good team. Exams are closed-book but not hard either if you go to review session. I learned lots of professional terms in these two courses.
I don't like this professor. Because she asks you to answer questions in class. I didn't know this percentage was significant until the end of the semester.
Caring professor. Class involves assignments and group projects. Not much busy work. Fair grader.

analysis.name: Yasuyuki Motoyama
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I thought he's been great so far. He isn't the best lecturer but once you get into his labs he makes sure students are able to follow along and stops a lot to help out. Responds to emails quickly and wants to make sure you succeed. Lab sessions were hard but easy to get help, assignments were alittle tough if you didnt fully understand the lab.
Motoyama is obviously super knowledgeable, but he isn't the best lecturer, which sucks even more because he doesn't post the slides. He made this class way harder than it should have been.

Dr. Motoyama is clearly knowledgeable in his field and is passionate about the material, just not passionate about teaching it. Labs are essentially follow-along lectures with no explanation or clarification. He will try to evade office hours. You will be learning the material on your own for projects. This class was harder than it should have been

Professor Motoyama is very knowledgable, but he was difficult to reach outside of class, and did not give great feedback. Lectures were interesting, and the projects were pretty easy. Sometimes class was boring.

Very focused on his own work and only does the minimal to teach students. Will refuse to expand on lectures. Expects students to know exactly what he want in reports and grades harshly if it's not correct. Doesn't respect students ideas or opinions.

analysis.name: Matthew Yde
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great.  Knowledgeable.  Great insights.  Excellent lectures.  I worked very hard in researching and performing in my final examination project.
Excellent professor.  Very motivational.  Clear directions.  Kindness.  You work very hard.
Interesting information.  Creative.  Kind.  Became newspaper theatre critic in later years.

Well-versed.  Informative.  Protege of Dr. Woods, and a fine disciple.  Great future for this talented instructor.  He is motivated to be a good teacher, as well as keeping a fine eye upon the stated objectives of the class.

Loved it. Matt is great and really well-versed in the subject matter. Though the class was nothing like what I thought it would be, I ended up really enjoying myself and getting quite a lot out of it.

analysis.name: Yana Hashamova
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr Hashamova is greatly interested in the material she teaches, students are encouraged to interact with word and film alike to explore topics. For an online course, there was a good level of interaction with the instructor and other students. I would recommend if this fits your degree plan.

Directions for quizzes are simple and she keeps things short. The class itself is really interesting. The media (movies) required for the course is entertaining but be ready to read. At first glance the readings seem daunting but the quiz that follows is usually easy.

This class was great. Not too much work but I feel like I did learn a lot about Russia. Most of the assignments are watching Russian movements/reading short stories or going though presentations and taking quizzes on them.

analysis.name: Alper Yilmaz
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Wonderful lecturer, material was really dry and was very dense but Dr. Yilmaz made it bearable and very clear cut. Gives lots of extra credit and you get to make your own cheat sheets for exams. I feel this professor cares and that's hard to come by these days. If you attend class and  take notes, no reason you shouldn't pass with at least a B.

Yilmaz is a great lecturer and cares a lot about the class. He can go at a pretty fast pace sometimes so it is easy to get lost if you aren't paying close attention. All of the homework, quizzes, and exams were online and he gives multiple attempts on exams. Easy A if you pay attention, take notes, and do the work

Professor Yilmaz is a relaxed instructor. In my experience, the course focused more on general concepts than civil engineering applications, which made parts of it less engaging for me. Lectures feel long, but attending helps with the labs. Not a super difficult class, just very long.

Tough class.  He tried every way he could to give students the benefit of the doubt.  Midterm is tough, he grades very easy, and final project you'll get an A just by turning it in. DO ALL the homeworks, even if you know you don't know how to do one...HW is 55% of the grade.  Don't buy the book, lecture notes are online.

Dr. YIlmaz is a really good guy. Really wants all of his students to understand and be interested in the topics he presents. Attendance isn't mandatory, but sometimes you will get rewarded with a bonus quiz or two. Homework and quizzes almost every week, but it prepares you for the exam.

analysis.name: Yiyu Wang
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I'm pretty sure he's fresh out of grad school, but I don't know. He rushes like crazy during lectures, and his accent makes him hard to understand, so you'll find yourself sometimes walking out having learned nothing. Tests are weighted very heavily, 20% per midterm (2 of them) and the final is worth 40%. He doesn't explain concepts well also.

Not a bad lecturer, but way too fast and need to be supplemented. He copies the textbook as notes. I self studied the whole 1st and 2nd midterm because he does not teach concepts at all. Also harsh grading, 80% is exams with relatively small curve. He gives very little time for exams too.

This class is horribly weighted and the exams are very unrealistic. He gives extremely little time to complete multiple problems that very well take over 10 minutes to complete each, making it impossible to even finish an exam.

Yiyu is a chill guy but it's evident he's new to teaching. I can't blame him for this but it's what's holding me back from me actually learning. Also the exams  make or break your grade so make sure to study for them.

analysis.name: Zoe Ashton

analysis.name: Adam Beckman

you have to read a book throughout the semester and take a quiz on it each week of a chapter or two. you have a lecture on mondays(not tested on), group project wednesdays(you only present every other week), quiz and discussion friday. hes really cool and knows a lot about the industry. if you miss a quiz its really easy to make up.

Really enjoyed this course with him, he works with students directly and really cares about students understanding the material. Definitely don't skip lecture, participation and attendance are heavy grades and some exam questions are based off lecture conversations rather than just notes. 10/10 loved having him as a professor!

The teacher is really nice and funny, but the class is a complete joke. Easiest A ever, however, you won't really learn much everything is repetitive, not marketing background. Slides are confusing, I was expecting to actually learn something about Airlines marketing. Take this class if you don't care about learning LOL

analysis.name: Adrian Calmettes
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I really enjoyed this class, the topics were interesting and the assignments and exams were easy if you keep up with the material. Reading load is normal for political science classes. He is a good lecturer and appreciates participation but I found it easy to participate, even though I usually do not speak much in class.

Professor Calmettes was good, be ready for lots of reading. There were two quizzes a week for the two readings, exams were easy, and attendance is an easy grade boost. Overall, he was very insightful and helpful.

I learned a lot from this class and it laid the foundation for my future upper-level polisci classes. Being ready to participate more in class requires reading articles that are not very long. The quizzes are not hard and you can find answers in assigned readings easily. Professor Calmettes is very caring and not a tough grader.

You'd get the most out of Calmette's class if you already have a lot of political science experience as the lectures are very complex and so are many of the jargon filled papers, he isn't always very brief. If you have that background though you can learn a lot and the grading is not harsh.

analysis.name: Aditya Chaudhry
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Chaudhry may be the Fisher Goat. Lectures were extremely engaging and easy to follow. Your grade is mainly determined by how well you do on the quizzes, midterm, and final, however I thought all of these were very fair tests. Another plus is that the homework is extremely easy and you still get credit for it. Highly recommend, great guy.

But his quizzes and exams were weighted 80% of your total grade and he did not know important details about how many questions the quizzes and exams had. The time limit of the final exam was not very clear either. He did curve in the end though.

He is a responsible lecturer and tries his best to help you understand the contents. And also he is accessible outside the classroom. However, his 2 exams and 2 quizzes weight about 80% of the grades. And some conceptual questions in exams are never covered in slides.

analysis.name: Adam Champion
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

review_highlights.comment: Possibly my least favorite professor I've had the mispleasure of having at OSU. The class only happens twice a week yet there's a pop quiz every two weeks that takes the entire period. The topics on these quizzes and midterms range from basic principles to gosh I hope you really remembered that one obscure detail that was talked about for 30seconds

Champion is a good person and seems to care a lot about his students. If you go to him during office hours, he is very helpful. The labs can be long, but they are very interesting and informative. However, his lectures don't really teach you much, and you have to rely on the textbooks to truly understand the topics covered.

Champion's lectures are extremely long, dry, and boring. He tends to talk at students for the entire lecture, and sometimes goes off on random tangents that contribute nothing. He is also not really knowledgeable about the material he assigns for labs, and can't provide helpful explanations/answers in lecture or office hours.

Champion is very smart and knows his stuff, but he has trouble dumbing down complex topics for people who have never seen it before. The class is very lecture and slides heavy and his lectures are very dry and hard to follow.

Adam is a nice guy, but he is a HORRIBLE teacher. Lectures are worthless but mandatory; however, you either stay for a 30 min lecture or have a "work day" most days. Nothing from his lectures will help with the group project or the exams. The textbook for the class is really good and is the only way to really learn the material to pass the class.

analysis.name: Adam Grupa
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Very knowledgeable guy, and a good teacher. Lecture was usually just going through slides, answering questions, and sometimes a funny or interesting story beforehand. I don't ask questions during class, but he created a good learning environment, and was also very helpful in office hours. Exams are hard, but he wasn't out to get you in grading.

It's actually insane how difficult his exams are compared to other Software 2 Professors. He gives absolutely no resources for exams, and barely reviews in class. Exams themselves are just the hardest coding questions possible back to back. If you get this guy make sure you put triple the amount of effort you normally would.

I genuinely GENUINELY believe that he doesn't want students to get good grades in his class. I mean he PURPOSEFULLY makes it so much harder than it has to be. He gives NO exam prep, his exams themselves are stupidly difficult and there's no curve or anything. He made the semester miserable for sure
Very passionate about computer science. If you attend his lectures and pay attention you'll do fine. Will take time both during and outside of class to help you.

My biggest issue with Adam is the lack of information provided to study for exams in a meaningful capacity accompanied with the fact that he never puts out his study info until the week of the exam. I would think with the overwhelming majority of the weight of the course being put on the exams we would get more to work with besides lecture slides.

analysis.name: Adil Ibrahim

(for 2221) it's obvious he knows what he's talking about but the lectures weren't very helpful and a chunk of his office hours were skipped for some reason or another. be prepared to use outside resources to learn the things you're expected to.

also, grades are HEAVILY weighted toward exams. i had a B+ before the final and got screwed over, lol

(For 2221), He usually doesn't reply to emails, his lectures are worse than other professors, exams are harder than other professors. In general, I don't know how to evaluate him.

analysis.name: Claire Adams
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

I'd rather take her class that one where I skate by and don't learn.

Claire was a great professor, truly cared about her students & always gave insightful meaningful feedback. I will say there is a lot of work, however it was all very informative and useful. By far one of the most beneficial classes I took in college. Also Claire is very knowledgable, & I loved learning from her. Really recommend taking this course!

not sure why Claire has all these bad reviews, I'm assuming she changed her Digital Marketing class because its mostly group work and activities. analysis.name: Ahmad Al-Jallad

Professor Al-Jallad is one of the most passionate professors whose passion is undoubtedly matched by their mastery of the subject. Lectures are thought-provoking and easy to follow. He's more concerned with making students just as fascinated he is than he is with assignments. Generous feedback and available for office hours with tea! Take him!

Best professor and best class at OSU by a million. Every class had very very high-level discussions which I could honestly never get anywhere. OSU needs to cherish Ahmad and this class and publicize it a lot more because I believe every Muslim or anyone interested in Islam NEEDS to take this course. He is a very light grader and very personable.
Def take him more for his lectures than any class work.

Great Professor and easy class!

analysis.name: Bob Ahern

Bob was the first professor I've had who has ever REALLY held my attention the entire course (which was surprising because our class was ~3.5 hours long!). Bob always connected the class back to his practice. He is one of the most realistic professors I've had thus far: I came out of his class knowing what to expect in the social work field. He is understanding and genuinely cares about student success. He always kept a 4 hour class interesting and had reasonable expectations for assignments.

Bob is the best professor I have had in my entire educational career. He is an easy grader, but he provides a lot of helpful and encouraging feedback. Not only does Bob tell you he cares about his students, he shows it as well. He's also hilarious. I wish he taught all of my courses because he's a great professor and a great person.

Amazing German teacher. He cares a ton about his students and their understanding. He speaks very clearly and wants his students to participate. Just don't get on your phone during class and he will like you. I had an A- and he rounded it up to an A for me without even having to ask. 10/10

Professor Abate is amazing, her class is set up very organized and deadlines are fair. She's a great person and has nice energy when teaching. 5 exams with averages around 80%. Got a 70 on the first one and was caught off guard since I didn't write down all information she mentioned, exams are pretty detailed. Says questions aren't tricks but they lowkey are. Overall, just make sure you attend every lecture and type every word.

I really liked this class with her. She makes the lectures interesting and is very clear on what will be tested. Everything in the class is pretty straightforward and she is very intelligible with all the topics. Exams are the majority of your grade, but they aren't too hard if you pay attention in lecture and write good notes.

Best professor I've ever had here. Her style of teaching was a bit crazy at times but she was always willing to go back and explain things as many times as we needed. Her stories during lecture are always hilarious and borderline crazy and she made attending lecture fun. Tests are fair, hard class and requires a lot of work but doable if you study.

Dr. Dunlevy goes right up to the top of my favorite professor list. Her whole attitude of "do less" and "I don't care" is brash, hysterical and relatable to college students. Did I mention she's also a good teacher and not just funny? Well, she is. Just because she says "I don't care" and cusses doesn't mean she hates her job. She's great. 11/10

analysis.name: Craig Franze

This professor was constantly late to class and did not respect his students time. He would make a fuss about students leaving lecture on time to get to other classes on time. I did appreciate his review sessions that he would provide before the exam. He was never actually present at exams. I felt as though my TA was a better teacher.

Avoid him if you can. He is so lazy with his teaching methods, and no accountability or improvement. People pay thousands of dollars to get a professor who reads off pre-made lecture slides on math. He doesn't teach in real time or go through examples; he comes up himself. you will sit there being lectured like it's English class instead of math.

Lectures consisted of the professor reading off slides, which allowed me to learn close to nothing. And she argued with us on matters of opinion for the rest of the semester. Don't take

she use course percentage to determine your final grade.. tough grader

Try your best to avoid this professor you will not learn majority of the material because you will be overwhelmed with the way she tries to explain the materials and the amount of homework she assigns
She has long pointless lectures and shows mostly proofs which dont really help me. said the tests weren't hard but she was clearly lying cause I failed the first exam...

analysis.name: Carla Curtis

Be prepared for VERY passive aggressive comments about your work. She responds to your opinions that disagree with hers and gives no parameters as to why she is disappointed in you. Group work is excessive- especially when online.

She is intelligent but a poor communicator. Only 3 assignments (2-pg paper & 2 exams) but be prepared to read (syllabus has 5 pg bibliography). I love Dr. Curtis. Textbook use is fairly high,although it is not really necessary - she can be a little scattered in her thoughts and reading the book helps to make everything fit together. Her assignments take a bit of time outside of class (and she does not use carmen) but i found it manageable with a full time and 2 other classes.

analysis.name: Jessica Cutshall

review_highlights.comment: Easy GPA booster class for 3 credit hours, I only spent like less than an hour completing the 2 weekly assignments. I turned in my final project late a bit but I got full credit and I am just happy she takes all late work.

Jessica was an awesome instructor! We had really interesting discussions in her class and the assignments were interesting. I have recommended this class to all of my  friends. Through the course I gained confidence in myself & truly feel like my college skills were improved. Love her!

analysis.name: Cubonova Lubomira

READ THE BOOK and REVIEW EVERY SLIDE/NOTE TO STUDY

Very exam heavy and your grade depends on tests. Exams are highly application based and don't match learning goals well. Hard if you're not a strong test taker. Exams aren't released and lectures aren't recorded, making it difficult to improve. Slides aren't very helpful.

I felt her lectures were beneficial along with the in class activities. You receive easy points by showing up and completing TopHat questions, so I would recommend going to class. She also points out important things to know and the TopHat questions are a good guide to study. Mastering biology was very difficult and for accuracy.

analysis.name: Emilie Curtis

By far the WORST professor Ive had during my academic career. Flexible about assignments/deadlines and good about responding to emails, but a ton of reading and assignments piled up towards end of semester- partly on me for not starting to work on those earlier tho. Also major assignments didn't seem like they were worth enough points for the effort required.

She is an amazing professor but there were times where I felt like I really didn't need to come to class. She was flexible on when assignments were but she also assigned a ridiculous amount of work at the end of the year and didn't really care that a lot of us are taking 4 other classes.

analysis.name: Curtis Haugtvedt

review_highlights.comment: If you are interested in going through 5 minutes of slides during class & then discussing current events or his/other students personal & often unrelated experiences, take Curts class. Class is almost entirely based off of Ted talks and his own anecdotes. Interesting guy who obviously cares a lot about consumer behavior but has little actual teaching ability mainly due to the fact that he is constantly cancelling class.

Not a bad instructor overall.  Nice guy, good lecturer.  Canceled our Friday class so it was just Monday Tuesday each week.  But in its place you have to write 3 discussion posts a week (kinda a lot - gets annoying)  There is a 15 - 20 page paper for the final, but you get to choose the topic so it is not completely terrible.

analysis.name: Cynthia Tyson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Exactly what you want from an online gen ed class. Just look up YouTube videos of read alouds of the picture book for the book reports. Super easy and can get the work done for the week in about 30 minutes. The final is a 5-7 page essay though, but since the rest of the class is a breeze you really can't complain about it.

I had this course online so it was really easy. You're just reading picture books and children's books and discussing what you learned from that week in a page-long summary, book report, or other assignment. She's not super fast at emailing back, but she was a chill professor, and it was an easy A. The only large assignment was the final essay.

I took Intro to Children's Literature, so you're discussing children's books and to make it better, Cynthia is very down to earth. She is funny and sassy which makes the class bearable. She expects you to be in class with the books read and work done, but overall its a fun class to take!

analysis.name: Cynthia Burack

review_highlights.comment: I really did not like Prof. Burack. Her lectures were incredibly boring, and although it was supposed to be a discussion-based class, she rarely let students get a word in. Cynthia is a very cool person. She clearly cares a lot about the subject and enjoys discussing it. The books assigned were great too and the readings were reasonable. I missed almost half of the discussion posts but still received an A- in the end, so she is very forgiving as a grader. I would recommend!

Expected to read a number of pieces, but they are all interesting and manageable. The only assignments are weekly discussion posts, which are graded pretty fairly. Attendance isn't mandatory, but I enjoyed going to class. Burack is extremely knowledgable and really just wanted to have open discussion (not mandatory) with the class!

Dr. Burack provided very relevant material to read. This was the first time that I actually read every. single. book. for a literature class and loved them all. There are about 6 papers that are one page each (double spaced) and a weekly discussion post--not too much work. Truly enjoyed the material and loved both her teaching and the class.

I felt like the exams were super easy, I can only remember missing one or two questions on each. Shes pretty straightforward about exam prep, but if you dont literally take notes during lecture, youre not going to do very well in the class. Felt like I deserved an A, but the grading criteria was not clear at all! Did not use Carmen at all!

I have mixed feelings about this professor. The class is a lot of group work which isn't bad if you have a good group. Dr. T is a dry lecturer but the material in this course is pretty straightforward. She requires the textbook but you could probably do well in the class without it, I didn't really read it. She wants to help you so if you have questions, she is receptive to them. 70% of the course is two exams and there are group quizzes and one group project.

She says it's her first time teaching this class so that's her excuse.

Amazing lecturer, made class interesting. Heavily reliant on readings but as long as you do most them, attend lectures, occaisonally participate, you should get an A. Dr. Clopper's class was amazing. The directions for assignments were always super clear, so if you show up to class and learn how to do what the assignments cover, getting a good grade is a breeze. She's great at explaining material several ways, and seems to genuinely care about her students.

Dr. Clopper is absolutely fantastic. She is organized, communicates and lectures clearly, and is truly invested in her students' success. She is always accessible and is just a wonderful person and professor. 11/10.

analysis.name: David Widdifield

Dr. Widdifield is a really knowledgable professor and you can tell he enjoys being able to teach and share his knowledge. The class and assignments weren't too hard at all. 10/10 professor who genuinely cares about his students and offers a lot of extra credit opportunities. There are optional lectures you can attend with guest speakers where you can also earn additional extra credit. Overall, a very good professor and a great class experience.

Absolutely amazing professor! Took BUSML 3380 all online with Professor Widdifield and it ran so smoothly. He was accessible outside of class and always quickly replied to my emails. Quite a few assignments due each week, the final was open book and not proctored.

analysis.name: David Thompson
