First time you meet her you will be thrown off guard but she is the best math TA and her class averages are always higher than all the others. i thought she was so good that i had her for 131 and then made sure i had her for 132 also. Always willing to help you and good at explaining things too. Only bad thing is that she has hard quizzes.

Jen is a trip! She's one of the most laid back TA's I've had in a long time. As long as you keep up on the homework, the quizzes are easy. She's more than willing to help or explain something if you don't understand it. The best were her nerdy examples and making fun of herself to lighten the mood of the class.

I actually learn more in recitation than I do in class. As long as you complete (and understand) the homework assignments, the quizzes are easy. If you have questions on anything, she's more than willing to answer, and explain until you understand what the f you're doing :)

I thought Jen did an amazing job teaching such a high level of calculus. I attribute my grade only to her since our lecturer for the course was pretty bad. shes a little laid back,and different, but is a very fair and just teacher. I would highly recommend her!

analysis.name: Jason DeWitt
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: (PHILOS2465) took this class to fulfill a GE, and it ended up being my favorite class I've ever had, most of the credit going to Jason's teaching. He is clearly passionate about what he teaches and tries to make each lecture and reading engaging and understandable. Super nice, was excited to go to class. Easy A if you pay attention and go to class.

PHIL 2332 Dr. DeWitt is a phenomenal professor. Would 100% recommend this course to anyone who needs it to satisfy a GE credit or for their major. This class is a gem in that it is not stressful or very taxing whatsoever but as long as you show up and pay attention, you will learn quite a lot as the lectures are super engaging, also just a cool guy

(PHIL2332) This was by far my favorite class I've taken. Professor DeWitt makes a 1hr 20 class go by fast, and his lectures are genuinely engaging. Even though attendance is mandatory, he allows 4 absences. Plus, his class was one I never wanted to skip, even though I skip class easily (for other classes). Very easy, yet I learned a lot. Take it!

Super chill dude, took Philosophy 2465 with him (wasn't listed on rate my professor for some reason) but yeah hes a good grader, very funny and makes the content very interesting. would recommend his class for a GE.

Loved DeWitt. Gives interesting lectures and makes it easy to participate. Fair grader and is willing to work with you- I was able to review my papers and got feedback that always helped me on the following ones. Pay attention in lectures and take some general notes and you will do well. Very much wish I could take him again- I learned a lot.

analysis.name: Kyle Dempsey
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: His class will be one of, if not the most difficult on your schedule. You will not do well in his class unless you participate, and I mean participate. Ask questions, attend office hours, etc. You can't just memorize the lecture slides and expect to do well in the course. Dempsey is very helpful and a skilled lecturer, but you have to be proactive.

Much like the other reviews say, Dempsey is a nice guy and is passionate about what he teaches. However, he does not translate the conceptual style of his lectures into solving economic problems (i.e. those on his exams) very well. You are only vaguely taught how to apply the material to the things that matter. He's OK but I don't recommend him.

This is a tough class. Dempsey does not write a lot of problems or give much practice material. He is not very accessible outside of class. During lecture, he spends too much time on simple concepts and speeds through the difficult material. You can learn enough to do well if you read the textbook and teach yourself.

I had Kyle Dempsey for ECON 4002.02 (Intermediate Macroeconomic Theory). The course consisted of one quiz, weekly problem sets, two midterm exams, and a final exam. The course was conducted online, and the midterm exams and final exam were proctored via Zoom. Prof. Dempsey was relatively unavailable outside of office hours. Doesn't allow appts.

I was highly impressed by Professor Dempsey especially since this was his first semester. He handled online classes extremely well and was always accessible. As for difficulty and grading, the top 15% of students received and A in my class. If you want to go to grad school for Econ, take Dempsey. He offers a true intro to real high level econ!

analysis.name: Debdipta Goswami
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Good guy mid prof tests are exactly the same as prac exams very bad at lecturing personally didnt go but still got As on the exams. better off using ai to teach you material but hes good at answering questions. Homeworks are kind of long and have little correlation to exams. Learn motor skills for each question on prac exam and youll be fine gudluc

His lectures can be somewhat boring but office hours were really helpful. Tests were easy but some homeworks can be a little tough. He also gave the opportunity to score lots of extra credits in tests. Also, very helpful in giving makeup exams and posting the lecture videos.
Doesn't have the most engaging lectures but tests are very easy. However, homeworks could take a while.
This guy is a huge racist. Avoid at all costs

He's alright. Lectures were very confusing or boring. There were a couple homework assignments that took some time, but he was very helpful in office hours and answered any question I had. Very smart guy.

analysis.name: Eric Danhart
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 124 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Engaging lectures, even though it was at 8am. As long as you go to class and pay attention, and keep up with the material, you will do well. Nice guy and always willing to help out in person or by email.

Super nice guy and professor, cares about your grade and wants you to learn (definitely isnt a I teach for an hour so I can pay for my research kind of guy). The textbook is nice but not necessary to get an A. His slides are an amazing study tool, though they can be a little unclear at times. Responds to emails quickly and very willing to help.
Tough class, but not too bad if you keep up with homework and stuff. Exams are tough, but there are lots of other points in the class to help your grade.

Professor Danhart was such a great professor. He likes using Tophat and in-class activities to help with your grade and also to see who does attend, but attendance isn't a mandatory thing. Just a fair warning if you skip this class, you will have a tough time passing exams because he makes his exams a little tougher in order to test your knowledge.

Dr. Danhart seems like a nice guy, but I genuinely don't know how anyone does well on these exams. They require an extremely deep understanding of 30+ learning objectives for each exam, a good understanding of the content is absolutely NOT enough to get higher than a 60%. Maybe consider your other options if you don't have 10+ hours a week to study

analysis.name: Andrzej Derdzinski
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 71 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The worst professor I have ever had. Yeah, I mean it. He is obviously very smart, But he makes every single thing complicated and just talks to student in his way. I basically learn stuff by myself for whole semester. In addition, he graded heavily on exams while every exam has only 4-6 questions. If you miss one, you are screwed.

Professor Derdzinski, while a brilliant mathematician, is simply a terrible teacher. He speaks directly into the board while lecturing, never stopping for input from students. If he stays on topic in lecture, it's a miracle - he flies through proofs without explaining any concepts. Midterms were 4 questions each, final was 6. Don't take his class.

If you choose to attend his lectures you will more than likely end up staring into space or sitting on your phone more than taking notes. He does not clearly and efficiently go over the topics that are on the tests in class and during recitation he discusses random topics that will never be needed. Basically you will teach yourself the course.

Quite possibly the worst professor I have ever had in my entire educational career. Lectures are abstract and worthless. No solutions are available for any of the practice problems, so you have no idea if you are doing anything right ever. Tests are very short and partial credit is non existent. Avoid if you don't want to take the class twice.

The guy very obviously is versed at what he teaches, but is pretty bad when it comes to actually transferring the information. Tests are few, weighty, and there is basically no partial credit (we had a group of ten students approach him on this matter, only to get a short and rude response). If you learn from practical examples, AVOID.

analysis.name: Richard Dick
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Let's just say that he lives up to his name....
Terrible professor. Often changes due dates for assignments and reaaranges syllabus at will. Difficult to understand and unwilling to help students.
Took soil bio. Horrible experience. Horrible prof. Do not take it he hates teaching

Dr. Dick is a very smart and kind man.  While this class is only graded by 3 exams and a paper, if you listen to lectures, take good notes, and attend office hours before exams you will be fine.  It is definitely a class that requires effort, but it is extremely interesting, and I learned an incredible amount in 7 weeks.

One of the hardest classes I've ever taken. Professor jumps around with little transition and is near impossible to understand in lectures. For an 8 week class gives 3 exams and term paper with little turn around time. Not only was the class itself hard but halfway through professor left for a trip to Africa, leaving lab professor behind to teach

analysis.name: Diana Kline
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are totally optional and not helpful. Lab time is also optional except for the 3 exams. I did all of the labs at my own pace and just went to the open lab if I needed help. If you can do the practice exams you'll do fine on the regular ones. All multiple choices so the labs are harder than the exams in my opinion.

Very easy class if you have any knowledge of Excel and Access. Lectures/lab days are optional and pre-labs have step by step instructions. If you have questions, Prof. Kline and the in-lab graders are happy to help you. Lots of busy work and 3 multiple choice exams that didn't require much studying.

The sweetest human ever! Very approachable and cares a lot about her students success. Being successful in the class just comes along with practice, but overall it wasnt that hard. Definitely recommend taking Dr. Kline!!

The lectures and class itself is kind of boring, but Professor Kline is a very caring and understanding person. There are usually 2 labs and 1 content quiz every week. There are 3 exams total and are all multiple choice. The lab time is optional (only go in if you need help). Overall would recommend!

Fairly easy class, stopped going to lectures after the first couple weeks, homework is just two labs and a quiz every week, nothing too difficult.  3 multiple choice exams, easy if you just look at the "study guide" given and know how to do the labs.

analysis.name: Melanie Dickman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: An insanely good prof. She was very easy to talk to and reach outside of class. It's a writing class, so get ready to write something weekly, but aside from that her grading criteria is exteremely clear and is very reasonable.

She's really personable and an easy grader, but there are A LOT of written assignments, which makes sense given the course. The papers are generally easy, and there's an automatic 24 hr extension on all assignments. There's a major group project at the end which is not a lot if you split up the work evenly, and no final exam/quizzes/tests.

I had professor Dickman for Aviation 2200. This class is a more literature heavy aviation class. Professor Dickman is a really easy grader, and you will do good as long as you put some sort of effort into the class. I would recommend not waiting till the last second to do your work, however.

Melanie is a great person, not so great professor. I put in little to no effort to receive an A in her class. Her modules were very unorganized and I struggled finding important information often. She is happy to help when given the chance, but teaching is not her calling. I was hoping to learn more from this class than I did.
I took AVN2300 with Professor Dickman, she knows her stuff and cares about her students. She is very approachable, and recommend taking any course with her.

analysis.name: Fernanda  Diaz-Basteris
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dra. Díaz-Basteris is one of my favorite professors thus far at OSU. She brings a unique perspective to the Spanish curriculum which is so valuable for a field that often forgets about the Caribbean and LatinX communities. Her lectures are engaging, and it's not hard to do well on assignments as long as you're engaged in class and put in effort.
This was a class I dreaded going to. I always felt anxious in her class and highly criticized. I would reccomend OSU students to find another class. It'll save you a lot of emotional energy.

Professor Diaz-Basteris created a safe space for all students which made me feel comfortable presenting as my full self in the classroom. I loved that she took us on trips beyond the classroom and that her assignments were tailored to help students develop skills beyond the classroom. Highly recommend her courses!

The professor made a point to connect the course material to contemporary events. In doing so, she made complex ideas accessible and demonstrated the use value of theoretical frameworks in day-to-day life.

I'm definitely taking other classes offered by this professor.

Dr. Diaz-Basteris's passion made class engaging and thought-provoking. Her diverse material and meaningful discussions deepened my understanding of the Caribbean. She truly cares about her students, making her an exceptional professor.

analysis.name: Kelly Fulkerson Dikuua
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Absolutely loved Dr. Fulkerson-Dikuua, she was more than happy to provide extensions when needed and is a pretty fair grader. If you read all the assigned readings for the week her class is a guaranteed A.
Her African American Studies class is really easy and she's a really caring teacher. Super understanding and a wonderful professor. Would schedule with her if u can

AMFAST 1111 actualy. Good professor, contains weekly 10 question quiz on assigned readings and films. Respond to weekly discussions critiquing peers projects. Also six, 250 word reflections on diverse African topics such as universities, articles, and social media, along with a significant project due at the start of a designated week. Good GenEd.

Kelly Jo was an overall great professor. Very understanding about deadlines, and offers extra credit for great thoughtful answers. Consistent assignments, you can expect a quiz and discussion each week (more). One paper, small project, and a major final project. Timely grader with the exception of major projects. Lectures are optional but helpful.

An angel honestly. Kelly Jo was one of the most caring, fair & balanced, and informative profs I had. I took two classes, wgss/afamast/compstd 4921 (intersections) and afamast 2367 (Black women writers), and she gave me extra credit points whenever she really liked my answer or could see that I put in a lot of effort. Take her classes!

analysis.name: Diana Padrutt
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Diana is great. Very funny. Because the class was online, participation and discussion were extremely important and worth a decent chunk of your grade, as you are graded on very few things. The class was 2 hrs and 15 mins and she had it go the entire time and rarely ended class early. There are also readings each week before class to read.

She was so amazing. I learned the most from this class than any other class I have taken in the social work program. She was clear, fast paced with lots of relevant content. She has good stories and fun classes that keep you entertained and understanding the content. Presentations are fun as well. Just loved this class!

Diana is amazing! She is a wealth of knowledge and she relates course materials to things she has experienced in the field. She surveyed the class the first night and adjusted a module to include what students wanted to learn. Her focus is more on ensuring we learn content than just getting a passing grade.
One of the best professors that I have ever had at OSU. She truly cares about the profession and her students. Absolutely amazing woman.
Not understanding of students going through difficult times.

analysis.name: Diana Sacilowski
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Sacilowski was honestly one of my favorite professors at OSU. She has incredible insight into Eastern Europe + good material that made understanding migration to the US easy. If I was confused on anything, she was always accessible at office hours and very helpful with feedback. She is a great professor and I highly recommend this class!
I've had her for Polish 1101, 1102, 1103, and Slavic 2230. In all of these she was never too difficult and lectures were always informative.

If you can take a class with this professor, do it! She is a kind individual and excellent at teaching. She teaches in a way that you genuinely learn the material. The lectures never drag on because she switches between different engaging activities throughout the class. Just take Polish!! It's a good class!

Slavic vampires is an amazing class that teaches you way more than you would expect and gives you two semesters worth of GR credit. You get to read about vampires with an amazing professor, what isnt to love????
While the readings and lectures could be long, Slavic Vampires was a very interesting class taught by a caring professor. The grading could be a little bit slow, but the content was great.

analysis.name: Deb Rumsey
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 245 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Rumsey is just an awful professor. The online homework is timed and graded by correctness so it's not homework at all, but a quiz. Youre thrown into recitations without having any practice and are expected to be able to answer questions correctly for a grade. There are stupid-nit picky rules that make the class a pain. Total joke of a professor

By far one of the worst, most annoying classes I've ever taken. Assignments take 4+ hours to complete and hard to tell what grade you'll get. Attendance is mandatory for pointless recitation while still expected to watch online lectures for the week. One of the most mentally draining classes I've taken. Material is fairly difficult, not impossible.

WATCH HER VIDEOS. gave up going to scheduled lecturer and switched to watching her posted lecture and they were great. Only took ~45 of watching to understand concepts for the week. TAs sucked and recitation is more of a free work period with mandatory attendance. If you want a good grade, watch her lecture vids and they cover all concepts on tests

Don't understand all the 5 star reviews. Is she really nice and caring? Yes, but does that translate to the class being enjoyable and understandable? No. The worksheets in recitation take quite a bit of time and it's a toss up on the grade you'll get on them. You won't learn anything in lecture, as she is a little all over the place when teaching

I took this class in person, but I just watched the online lectures, which were really helpful. Attendance for recitation is required, but you get 4 excused absences. Recitation assignments take a really long time. I find Professor Rumsey's online lectures more helpful than in-person personally.

analysis.name: Donald Soles
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Donald Soles, or "Donny" as he prefers to be called, is definitely the best professor I've had so far. He is super funny, flexible with due dates, liberally available, and genuinely wants his students to succeed. He also writes you a letter of recommendation to law school if you receive an "A". I am currently in his 3410 class, and it's great.

He really rewards effort. If you do the readings and come to class, it's pretty easy to do well even if philosophy isn't really your thing. He makes it harder to get a solid A, but if you get an A he'll write you a letter of rec for law school. He's good about being there for students and he definitely will help you improve if you make an effort.

Donny is a super nice prof and genuinely wants the best for you. that being said, the class is based off of 3-4 big assignments so make sure to put effort into those. instructions can be very vague and there aren't rubrics, but if you ask questions he will tell you exactly what he expects. Effort goes a long way with this guy so work for your grade

Donny was pretty chill, and his lectures were interesting when he let the class discuss stuff. Sometimes it seems like he likes to hear himself talk, but that's not always a bad thing (he can be entertaining lol). 
Participate in his class, put effort into the essays, read at least a few of the readings, and it's smooth sailing.

One of the best professors I have ever had. So insanely understanding and easy-going. Very laid back and truly wants you to do well and see you succeed. Have so much respect for him, such an amazing guy.

analysis.name: Khosrow Doroodian
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Would not recommend, making us show up to a Zoom call at 8 am on a snow day; the whole school, other than him, had recorded lectures, not him. We sat in an empty Zoom call, and he couldn't even figure it out for 25 minutes. Literally every assignment had issues with it at some point, and he could not remedy these issues in any capacity.

I missed a quiz because I was taking care of my mom in her 60s. She had hurt herself and asked me to come home and help her out while she rested. He ignored my email asking him if I could take it a few days later. Come to find out, he allowed another student who was "going out of town" to take the quiz. This quiz was worth 12% of my grade.

He does not respond to emails whatsoever and is very difficult to communicate with. Takes days/weeks to answer and to even get a response you need to email him 45 times. If there is a technical issue, he basically says he can't do anything about it and is very reluctant when it comes to accommodating.

One of the best classes I've taken in Fisher. He does cold call, but in a small class everyone was called on, if you don't know the answer he'll tell you instantly. The class is really interesting and as someone with a short attention span, I paid attention a lot. He cares about students success. 
Hard but pay attention and you'll succeed.

Quite literally the worst professor I've ever had in college. He makes 80% of the class worth of exams for an online class. It would not be as bad if it was open note, but he makes this class that is supposed to be easy much harder than it needs to be. Run away and choose somebody else!

analysis.name: Dmitri Kudryashov
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Hardest class I have taken. Exams are over 200-400 slides and he expects you to memorize every thing on every slide; and the exams are all fill in. Lectures are impossible to keep up with as he spends no more then 30 seconds on each slide. Good Luck.

Dr. Kudryashov really cares about his students. He is constantly sneaking in little comments about good study habits and eating properly (in terms of biochemistry). The content is challenging, but doable if material is kept up with. Tests are fair, and Kudryashov is more than willing to help struggling students.

Dr. Kudryashov was an excellent professor. However, I believe we tried to cover too many topics in the semester. This being said, everything he tested us over was very fair. What made the class difficult was the fact you needed to know almost EVERYTHING.  If you keep up, study weekly with the material, and understand concepts you will do very well.

Very hard professor. Took 4 exams total, all of which felt like finals (2 hours long all extended response quetions). He would tell you to memorize basically everything. Unneccessarily hard exams. Looks for very particular answers. Overall, this class is one of the most challenging I have taken, I recommend the other professor instead of Dr. K.

Kudryashov is the best! One of the rare ones at OSU who really cares about the students success and not only about their research. The material is very challenging, but like any science class, you won't be handed an A. In short, he makes class enjoyable and this Russian accent makes things a lot more interesting to listen to! I recommend.

analysis.name: Sarah Douglas
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Her class has 5 book dissections/reports, heavy reading, discussion boards with foot citations. Very tough grader. Not an easy A at all. Even if you think you're working hard, you have to work harder. Power points are nothing but her just speaking.

Her lectures are very instructive, did a good job considering short session. She does have long lectures, advise taking breaks or speed up. Accessible and understanding though, homework is mostly discussion boards and quizzes that can be retaken once. 1 research writing as a final. Not bad for me but others could be overwhelmed.

The class is very lecture heavy but its balanced with a reasonable workload of assignments. She can be somewhat of a tough grader and just about never gives perfect scores but is usually reasonable. Textbook was technically required but not necessary to get a good grade in the class with how dense the online lectures are.

She is very upfront on the amount of work this class demands. I loved watching her lectures. Quizzes were pretty straight forward and you get two attempts. If you go in expecting to get an A with minimal work you will be caught off guard, but if you understand this is a half semester 3000 level class, you will like the course.

The class was a second session course, so she expected to get two weeks of material done in one week. While doing this you are expected to spend a majority of your week, reading and writing for her. Her TAs are also the harshest graders Ive ever had.

analysis.name: Ellen Dossey
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This course is very difficult. She is a tough grader. This course is really not a shui ke.

The lectures can feel long at times, but the professor makes the material approachable and easy to understand. Although the class is online, quizzes and exams are challenging due to extended response questions. Overall, I learned a lot and recommend engaging deeply with the material.

Dr. Dossey is average professor.  She is pretty easy to reach outside of class but takes points off for dumbest reasons possible.  The class was also harder then it needed to be as someone who went to every lecture.  Overall she is a fine teacher
a lot of readings, not hard though

She does a great job in fostering a caring atmosphere for her students. I learned more in this class in one month than some of my other core classes the entire semester. You have to write a few essays but she does a great job with everything.

analysis.name: Douglas Alsdorf
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 77 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Alsdorf is a decent professor and attempts to make a dry subject bearable but tries too hard to be funny. If you're not an earth science major, I recommend avoiding this class. Not sure, why people say it's an easy "A". His exams are not straight forward and lies when he says everything he mentions will be on the test. PSA: avoid this professor

Doug is a real "dad" professor. His class is difficult, and you HAVE to go to lecture to do well on exams; but because of how hilarious he is, you won't want to skip. No textbook! He gives you a bunch of life advice within his lecture. Make sure you go and take notes. i recorded every lecture and that helped.

Very relaxed. All his lectures are like listening to your "funny" uncle talk. Nothing hard about the class. Every lecture is recorded online and he explicitly talks about every question on each test during lecture. Seven exams the lowest two dropped. Gives the answers to the final so make sure you attend the last lecture of the semester. Easy A.

No homework ever. Class grade based on labs (super easy) & 4 exams. Alsdorf will literally give you test questions in class&loves answering students' questions. Study slides & take notes of test questions and you'll do well on the exams. He really cares about his students&I found his lectures interesting & easy to follow. Really nice and funny guy

Took this class WI '11; Doug is a funny professor, definitely makes ES way more interesting than it is. His class is not "rocks for jocks" easy, however, and his expectations aren't clear; tests are often different than his notes and lectures. Gave a lot of outside material to help us understand concepts. Overall, a good professor for a GEC course

analysis.name: Matthew Dreher
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Dreher is a very kind person who truly cares and looks after his students.  He offered me a makeup exam after I was going through some hard times.  Overall, I would recommend him to anyone!
Attendance mandatory per FAA requirement. Very good instructor. Super nice and more than willing to help if you have any issues.

Matt is a good instructor. He is a little soft-spoken, but he always makes sure that you can hear. The grading for his class is black and white. USE THE ASA TEST PREP BOOK. It's like $12 and the questions on every assignment are taken directly from that book. The class is easy if you just listen to what he teaches.

Matt is great! If you want to fly with OSU, just take his ground school class. He gives lots of helpful stuffs and helps you prepare for the FAA test. Exams are just from prep book. He cares his students and answers all the questions!

This wasn't a traditional class. This was for the aviation spring break study abroad trip. Professor Dreher did a great job preparing us for our trip to France & Spain. Before we left, we learned about aviation history in the two countries. When were there he did a great job making sure that everything went well. Overall, it was a fun experience.

analysis.name: Suliman Dregia
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He doesn't mean to have such a bad attitude. Although, it was inbred.

Final was published 10 mins late, he was rude and dismissive of students questions and we didn't even get the 10 mins back. Unprepared to teach from day 1, this class was online and wasn't published until the first day of class. There were only 2 grades in the class, the midterm and the final because he didn't want to hire a TA to grade hw.
stank ass attitude towards teaching

Three months into the course, our only assignments are one midterm and two quizzes, for a total of 22 multiple choice questions. The questions themselves aren't terribly tough - but they're so specific to Dregia's lectures and found nowhere in his lecture notes or the textbook. The only way to do well is to religiously write down every Dregia rant

One of the worst professors I've ever had. He's the only one that teaches a mandatory MSE class, so you just have to deal with it. The lecture slides and the homeworks, quizzes, and exams he posts don't help at all. If you have him and want a B or better, you better sit in the front row and copy every little thing he says and writes on the board.
